waec-geography-theory-0054.explanation: (a) Meaning of Igneous Rock It is a type of rock formed from the cooling and solidification of molten magma. (b) Characteristics of igneous rocks - non-stratified - crystalline - not contain fossils - usually hard - Impervious/compact - some are jointed - either acidic or basic (c) Economic importance of igneous rock - source of energy (nuclear and geothermal energy) - soil formation - source of minerals - tourist attraction - source of raw materials for industries - as ornamental - for construction purposes

waec-geography-theory-0055.explanation: (a) Conditions that favour the development of karst topography: - Limestone should be the dominant surface rock -presence of joints/cracks/fissures/ bedding planes on existing rocks - The area should receive moderate to abundant and regular rainfall - The limestone area should be underlain by resistant rock - soluble rocks e.g. dolomite, gypsum, limestone - Surface relief should be low -tectonic activity will create cracks and joints Characteristics and mode of formation of sinkhole Characteristics - found in limestone regions - saucer-shaped or shaft-like depression - steep sided - could be shallow or deep - can be as deep as 20 meters or more - usually links the surface to the underground streams - water passes through it to the underground - can be 6 meters wide or more at the surface - varies in size and depth - Examples are found in the Atlas of Morocco, Ghyll in Yorkshire Mode of formation - formed in the karst region - presence of a large area of limestone with many cracks and joints - rain water mixes with carbon dioxide t • form carbonic acid - Acid dissolves the limestone along the cracks - The acidic run off passes through the limestone joints and cracks - The racks continue to deepen and widen. - The cracks are further deepened to become depressions called sink holes - two or more sink holes can be merged to form a do line Alternatively, the formation could also be sudden - Underground caves and voids are common in the limestone region - The roof of the cave may continue to recede or wear out - The recession continues for a long time - The cave roof collapses to form a hollow - This hollow is called a sinkhole - Moreover, mining activities could create a hole linking the surface to an Underground void or cave - Other human activities could cause the Substance of the cave roof to form sinkhole

waec-geography-theory-0056.explanation: (a) Identification of the types of climate using Koppen's system of classification (i) Af-Tropical rain forest climate (i) Am -Tropical monsoon climate (iii) Aw-Tropical grassland/savanna climate (b) Characteristics of the Af climate - located in the Tropics - located between 5°N and 5°S of the Equator - found in the coast of West Africa, Amazon Basin, Congo Basin, etc. - temperatures are uniformly high throughout the ye - mean monthly temperature is about 27 °C - annual range of temperature is shout 3ºC - there is high cloud cover - annual rainfall is between 1500mm and 2600mm

waec-geography-theory-0057.explanation: (a) Features that can be found in the middle course of a river - meander - interlocking spurs - river terraces - wide V-shaped valley - bluff - river cliffs - slip-off slope (b) Characteristics and mode of formation of a pothole Characteristics - found in the upper course of à river - found on the bed of a river - circular depression/bowl-shaped - cylindrical in shape - may be small or large - may enlarge and join to form a gorge - may be about 6 meters in diameter - may be about 15 meters in depth - greater in depth than in width - A plunge pool at the base of a waterfall is in a pothole - are exposed in the dry season when the river decreases - example: Devil's cauldron on the* River Congo Mode of formation - formed in the upper course of a river - formed on the riverbed - formed where the riverbed is uneven - A river loaded with pebbles flows in eddies when it reaches an uneven bed - The eddies cause the pebbles to swirl - This creates small shallow depressions on the river bed - River abrasion widens the depression to form cavities - cavities gradually deepen and widen - forming a feature called a pothole - Pothole: development depends on the nature of the bedrock and the speed of flow of the river - diagram.

waec-geography-theory-0058.explanation: (a)(i) The characteristics of a delta include: (i) The branching of rivers into channels called distributaries (ii) Large deposits of weathered materials (iii) It is formed at the mouth of rivers (iv) It takes up the shape of a fan (b) The r of formation of a delta is influenced by the following factors; (i) Active vertical and lateral erosion in the upper course of the river to provide extensive sediments to be deposited as deltas (ii) The coast should be sheltered or tic', (iii) The sea adjoining the delta should be shallow or else the load will disappear in the deep waters (iv), Absence of lakes in the river course to filter off the sediments (v) Absence of strong current running at right angles to the mouth so as not to wash away sediments (b)(i) Characteristics of caldera: (i) It is formed from volcanic activities (ii) It is a depression on volcano cones with steep sides (iii) Depression of magma gives rise to caldera (iv) It may contain water called caldera lake. Caldera is formed when composite volcano explodes violently, its top is blown off and disintegrates into a mass of rocks and ashes, leaving the crater greatly enlarged. The huge crater-like depression is coiled caldera. It can also be formed through subsidence. The depression may result in accumulation of water to form caldera lake

waec-geography-theory-0059.explanation: (a)(i) Annual range of temperature for the station is 21°C - 13°C = 8°C OR 70°F - 55°F = 15°F (ii) Annual Rainfall (Add all the precipitation from January to December = 642mm (or 25. 3 inches) (b) The distribution of rainfall in the station is such that the peak of rainfall is around June with the least in February. increases from January gradually till the peak in June and continues to decline till December. (c) The type of climate trend presented by the climatic table is Tropical Continental (Sudan type) Reasons: (i) The annual range of temperature is 8°C (ii) Only one peak of rainfall in June (iii) Decrease in rainfall early and late in the year. (d) (i) The type of natural vegetation is savanna:-Tropical Grassland (ii) The main characteristics of the vegetation are: (a) Presence of tall grass (b) Presence of scattered trees (c) Deciduous nature of the trees (d) Presence of trees like baobab, acacial etc.

waec-geography-theory-0060.explanation: (a) Three types of mountains are: (i) Block mountain e.g the Hunstruck mt. of Germany (ii) Fold mountain e.g the Himalayas (iii) Volcanic mountain, e.g Fuji mountain of Japan (b) Mode of formation of Fold mountains (i) Folding is caused by large stale h Drizontal earth movement (ii) Stresses, caused by expansion or contraction of some parts of the earth, are set up in the earth's crust (iii) Such stresses subject the reeks to compressive forces (iv) The compressive forces produce wrinkling or folding of the earth's crust (v) The upfold of the wrinkles are called anticlines while the downfold are synclines. (c) Four ways in which mountains are of great importance to man; (i) High mountain can result in the formation of rainfall i.e relief rainfall (ii) Mountain serves as the source or origin of all rivers (iii) Mountains are rich sources of minerals Stones found in mountains can be quarried for building construction

waec-geography-theory-0061.explanation: (a)(i) Two types of soil erosion are; (i) Water erosion and Wind erosion (ii) The area where water erosion is most common is moist humid area of the tropic (i.e rainforest areas), while wind erosion is common in the arid and semi arid areas especially in the desert (b) Three factors responsible for water erosion are (i) Excessive rainfall (ii) Impervious nature of underlying rock (iii) Increase in declivity (slope). The greater the slope, the greater the velocity and degree of erosion. (c) Three measures being taken to solve the problem of soil erosion in tropical area of the world are: (i) Contour ploughing. This involves the making of ridges across the slope to reduce surface run off (ii) Strip cropping: In slopy areas, strip cropping is done to also reduce the surface run off of the water (iii) Proper channelisation. This involves the construction of gutters to channel away the large volume of water caused by erosion

waec-geography-theory-0062.explanation: (a) Factors responsible for the very high population density in North - East of USA are: (i) Presence of great deposits of iron and coal (ii) Location of many industries (iii) Favourable climate conducive for human habitation (iv)Availability of jobs which make population to increase (iv) Heavy trading of manufactured goods within and outside the industrial zone of USA. (b) Factors which favour the high population density in the Indus and Ganges deltas (i) Abundance of rainfall which ensures smooth agricultural activities (ii) The soils are very fertile (iii) Intensive agricultural activities attract people to the area (they grow 2-3 crops in a year) (iv) Favourable climate conducive for intensive farming.

waec-geography-theory-0063.explanation: (a) Definition of atmospheric resources Elements found in the atmosphere that are useful to mankind, plants, and animals . (b) Importance of atmospheric resources - carbon dioxide for photosynthesis - Sunlight facilitates photosynthesis - Oxygen for respiration - Control temperature on the Earth's surface - sunlight for vitamin D (c) Human activities that adversely affect the composition of the atmosphere - The use of fossil fuels - deforestation - release of toxic wastes - bush burning - industrial activities - mining and construction - warfare - aviation - burning of tyres.

waec-geography-theory-0064.explanation: (a) Similarities between road and railway as major means of transportation are (i) Both road and railway are located on land (ii) Both are relatively cheap (iii) Both can be used to transport people and goods from one place to another (b) Differences between transportation by road and railway Transportation by Road Transportation by rail (1) Provides door-to-door service (2) It can only cover short distances (3) Carries mainly passengers (4) Less expensive to construct and maintain (5) It serves mainly residential areas - Does not provide door-to-door service - It can cover very long distances - Carries mainly goods especially agricultural and mineral products - More expensive to construct and maintain - It serves mainly industrial and agricultural areas

waec-geography-theory-0065.explanation: (a) Six factors which have favoured the development of Iron and Steel industry in the Ruhr region (i) Availability of coal which provides cheap source of coke for processing iron ore (ii) Availability of Iron ore (iii) Presence of Rhine which is one of the most navigable rivers in Europe, enables raw materials and goods to be moved between North Sea and Ruhr region (iv) Good network of excellent roads linking Rhine valley with the rest of West Germany (v) Abundance of soft, clear water (vi) By-products of Iron and steel industry leads to the development of chemical industries (b) Six factors which have favoured the development of Textile industries in Great Britain; (i) Availability of raw materials, e.g cotton, wool, silk and linen etc. (ii) Presence of coal which makes it possible for steam power to replace water power (iii) Abundance of soft water which is essential to removing the grease from wool before it is spun (iv) Abundance of skilled labour (v) Availability of large market (vi) Well developed centres and ports for the export of textile.

waec-geography-theory-0066.explanation: Three types of urban settlement include: (i) Cities (ii) Conurbation (iii) Megalopolis (i) City: A city is made up of large towns with great( number of people and services. In a city there are towns which combined together to function as one (ii) Conurbation: Is made up of two or more towns join E together through growth but which may still retain thE identities. These two towns are separated from eac other but through expansion or growth have joined together. But despite this, they still retain their identities (iii) Megalopolis: This is the largest of tl-urban settlements and includes the joining of man cities to form an extensive urban area. (b) Four problems of urbanization include: (i) Inadequate transport facilities. Increase in the number of people in the urban area often leads to problem of transportation (ii) Overuse and deterioration of available social services. Most of the social services available,. e.g electricity, stadium, school, hospital are overused and this leads to their deterioration (iii) There is an aggravated problem of unemployment and underemployment in the cities as well as reduce labour force in the rural areas (iv) There is the problem of undue increase in human and vehicular traffic.

waec-geography-theory-0067.explanation: (a) Four reasons why countries exchange goods and services (i) Natural resources; Natural resources of the world are unevenly distributed e.g Nigeria's petroleum is sold to Brazil in exchange for vehicles, sugar and communication equipment. (ii) Degree of Industrial Development; Due to high technical knowledge and expertise which a country has in the production of goods and electronic equipment than other countries e.g Japan specialises in the production of electronic equipment (iii) Some crops are more suited to certain climatic condition. Crops like cocoa, cotton, etc, grow in tropical regions while crops like wheat, barley and oats grow well in temperate regions (iv) Geographical Situation; Some countries have situations which enable them to take part in trade between contrasting economies e.g Singapore handles much of South East Asia's trade (b) Reasons for low volume of trade between Nigeria and the rest of Africa are (i) African countries produce goods which are very similar, leaving little or no room for exchange (ii) Nigerians have a high taste for imported goods from foreign countries. These goods are not produced by other African countries (iii) Nigeria's foreign exchange earnings from African countries is very low - about 20% (iv) Prices of goods offered by African countries are usually very low compared with foreign countries (v) African countries demand for very low quantity of goods unlike foreign countries.

waec-geography-theory-0068.explanation: (b) Four factors which have helped in the development of Apapa (Lagos) port; (i)Apapa port handles the bulk of the country's export and imports (ii) Apapa port is the focus of many different types of routes e.g sea routes from Europe (iii) it is served by good roads and railway network (iv) Apapa port is located on a very good harbour. (c) Two factors that have limited the use of Apapa port are: (i) Congestion of both importer: and exportable goods (ii) Drifting of sand and waves into the harbour.

waec-geography-theory-0069.explanation: (b) Effects of climate on the rainforest belt: (i) High rainfall the year round makes the vegetation to be evergreen (ii) High temperature also contributes to the vegetative growth of plants (iii) Abundance of sunshine and high relative humidity also contribute to the luxuriant growth cf forest trees. (c) Two resources found in rainforests are: (i) Timber - Used in the construction of houses and furniture -Timber can also be used as fuel wood (ii) Wild animals - Used as food, e.g bush meat - Serves as game

waec-geography-theory-0070.explanation: (b) Four reasons for high population density of Lagos (i) Lagos is a commercial town - heavy trading and presence of banks (ii) Presence of industries (iii) Availability of employment (or jobs) (iv) Lagos had been the Federal Capital. Four reasons for low population of Makurdi (i) Problems created by trans-Saharan slave trade (ii) Presence of tse-tse flies and black flies associated with sleeping sickness and blindness respectively (iii) Absence of social amenities (iv) Absence of mineral resources and industries.

waec-geography-theory-0071.explanation: (b) Importance of river basins in the development of Nigeria; (i) Most of the river basins serve as fertile ground for the cultivation of many crops e.g Chad basin (ii) Basins being lowland are good sites for human habitation i.e settlement (iii) Some water bodies in these basins are used for irrigation purposes (c) Three factors limiting the use of river basins; (i) Swampy nature of the area (ii) Inaccessibility of the area (iii) Seasonality of some of the rivers.

waec-geography-theory-0072.explanation: (b) Four ways in which cocoa is important to me economy of Nigeria (i) Cocoa provides foreign exchange for the country (ii) It is used in making beverages e.g, Bournvita (iii) It provides raw materials, e.g cocoa for industries (iv) It also provides employments to some people involved in cocoa production (c) There problems facing the cultivation of cocoa (i) The problem of pests and diseases (ii) Poor processing of cocoa beans (iii) Poor quality of cocoa species, some are low yielding.

waec-geography-theory-0073.explanation: (b) Rubber is produced or extracted from the tre( a process called tapping. Early in the morning rubber farmer goes to tap his rubber trees by making a cut on them. Below each cut he places a cup it which the milky juice caked latex drips. This is collected in pails in the evening. The latex is mixed with certain chemicals which make it to coagulate. it is rolled into sheets and smoked to a brown colt and are later sold to local buying agents. (c) Three problems which may hinder the large scale production of rubber include: (i) It takes the rubber trees long to mature - about 6 to 8 years (ii) Presence of poor quality or low yielding varieties of rubber (iii) Pests diseases attack on rubber also reduces the yield

waec-geography-theory-0074.explanation: (b) Three ways in which lumbering is important to West Africa countries (i) Export of timber earns foreign exchange (ii) Lumbering provides employment to many people (iii) Lumbering provides timber used in building construct and furniture (c) Three problems resulting from the exploit of timber resources in West Africa (i) Heterogeneous nature of trees (ii) Lack of motorable roads (iii) High cost of survey determine economic trees acceptable to foreign markets

waec-geography-theory-0075.explanation: (a) Important fishing areas and fishing ports in South Africa. Fishing is done in two ways (i) Inland fishing- not very popular and it is only done in Rivers Orange and Great Fish River (ii) Offshore fishing - Done along the entire coast of South Africa and also in deep seas i.e Atlantic and Indian oceans. Some of the fishing ports are port Elizabeth, Durban, East London. (b) Methods of fishing. On a large scale the method of fishing involves-the use of trawlers especially in the oceans (c) Major type of fish caught. These include mackerel, herring, salmon, had etc. (d) Preparation and marketing of fish. Fish caught are cleaned, refrigerated in cold stores and can be exp as raw fish. It can also be processed into usable canfish e.g sardines which are later consumed locally or exported (e) Fishing is very important for the following reasons: (i) It provides rich source of protein for the people (ii) Its exportation provides foreign exchange earning for the country (iii) It also provides jobs for many people (iv) It has resulted in the establishment of fish processing industries.

waec-geography-theory-0076.explanation: (a) Characteristics of plantation agriculture in East Africa (i) Plantation agriculture requires a large area of land (ii) There should be large supply of cheap unskilled labour within the location of the plantation (iii) Huge amok capital is required (iv) Infrastructural facilities like good roads, electricity, pipe born water are required (v) There be available skilled manpower (vi) Modern farming techniques are used e.g use of chemicals, fertilizer etc. (b) Pastoral nomadism in West Africa: (i) It requires the movement of cattle with their herdsmen from one play another in search of pasture and water (ii) It is more extensive than intensive method of cattle rearing (iii) Thi herdsmen are illiterate as they do not know how to treat diseased animals (iv) The cattle are subjected to love of feeding (v) There is the constant clashes between cattle rearers and arable farmers. (c) Fruit farming in South Africa (i) Fruit farming is made possible as a result of favourable climate and this includes bright and sunny weather, rainfall of 500- 700mm and temperature of 28°C (ii) Availability of fertile valleys where animal soil ex (iii) Funds must be made available to boost production (iv) Irrigation system is necessary for fruit farming (v) the fruits produced have access to foreign markets.

waec-geography-theory-0077.explanation: (a) Major areas of petroleum mining in North Africa include Libya, Algeria, Egypt and Tunisia (b) Methods of r petroleum involves drilling (i) The underground rocks are sampled and tested for traces of oil (ii) When oil is disco a well is sunk to reach it by the help of a drilling rig or derrick (iii) The oil is then pumped out, but where the enough pressure underground, the oil flows out on its own (iv) A system of values called "Christmas tree" is ei to control the flow into tanks (c) Transportation: Oil is usually transported through pipelines to the refineries tankers at the oil terminals can also be used in transportation of crude oil. (d) Importance to the economy: (i) provides foreign exchange earnings to the economy (ii) It is refined to obtain petrol, gas, kerosene, etc (iii) B products are used in making insecticides, petroleum jelly, lubricating oil etc (iv) Petroleum provides raw mater associated industries (v) It provides gainful employment to some people

waec-geography-theory-0078.explanation: (a) The characteristics of the following are; (i) Granite (i) Granite contains large crystals (ii) They do not occur in layers or strata (iii) They do not contain fossils which are the remains of plants and animals embedded in rocks. Limestone: (i) Limestone is arranged in layers or stata (ii) They contain fossils (iii) The rock is non-crystaline in structure (iii)Graphite: (i) Graphite is not crystaline (ii) It is arranged in layers or strata (iii) It may contain fossils (b)(i) Granite is formed from the cooling and solidification of molten magma ejected from below the earth crust. It cools before reaching the surface of the earth hence granite is called a plutonic or intrusive igneous rock (ii) Limestone is formed from the remains of living organisms such as corals or shellfish. These remains have been cemented together under the influence of water to form organic sedimentary rock (iii) Graphite is formed from pre-existing sedimentary rock called clay which have changed or metamorphosed to a new rock as a result of the influence of heat and pressure. Graphite is an example of metamorphic rock.

waec-geography-theory-0079.explanation: (a) Land And Sca Freezes: Breeze exchange between the land and the sea is attributed to differential heating of land and sea. These local wind are common in areas very close to the sea. During the day, the land is heated much faster than the sea and it is cooler than the sea at night. As the land is heated during the day, it causes the air to rise, creating a low pressure situation. Air therefore blows from the sea to replace the heated and rising air on the land thereby resulting in lower temperature and relatively cool air on the land. This is sea breeze which blows from sea to land. At night, the land becomes cooler that-. the sea having lost much of its temperature at a much faster rate than the sea. Thus, there is a high pressure situation on the land and a relatively low pressure situation on the sea. Hence a land breeze blows from the land to the sea. (b) Temperati.re inversion: This is the opposite of lapse rate and it means a rise in temperature with increasing altitude. It is not in all cases that temperature decreases with altitude. Temperature could be lower at the sea-level especially in valleys almost enclosed by mountains than at heights above such valley E.g temperature inversion is found in European Alps where cold and heavy al: collects in valleys which are almost totally enclosed by mountains (c) Convectional rainfall: This is the main type of rainfall in the humid tropics. The heat generated by the sun is aL;le to make the surroundings including the sea and ocean to be hot. Because the air is hot, it is able to absorb very large amount of moisture. The warm and moist air is forced to rise rapidly by convection current. When the current rises very high and reaches the cold layers of the atmosphere which make it conducive for the moisture contained in tha currents to condense, rainfall immediately fo: ows the condensation of the moisture. This type of rain formed by this process is called convectional rainfall.

waec-geography-theory-0080.explanation: The important features of Koppen; climatic classification is based on vegetation. It attempts to explain the variation of earth's climate by studying the connection between vegetation and climate. Koppean's classification of climates consists of five major climatic groups which are A- This is moist and hot climate e.g tropical rainy climates with avenge mz.nthly temperature of above 18°C. This climate has no winter seasons. Annual rainfall is large and exceeds annual evaporation. B - This is dry climate in which potential evaporation exceeds precipitation. Since there is no water surplus, no permanent streams originate in B climatic zones. C - This refers to moist and warm climate e.g warm temperate climate, whose coldest month has an average temperatures of under 18°C but has above 3°C in at least one month. It has both summer and winter seasons. D - This is snowy and cold climate (cold - snow forest climate). The average temperature of its coldest month is under 3°C. The average temperature of the warmest month is above 10°C E -This is polar icy climate (snow climate). The average temperature of its warmest month is below 10°C. This climate has no true summer. In order to differentiate between sub-divisions within these major groups, secondary letters are assigned to furnish more complete explanation e.g F - moist all year M -monsoon conditions S - dry summer wet winter V - dry winter, wet summer. A third letter was added to include information about temperature e.g a - long hot su. rimer b - short, warm summer c - short and moderate or cool summer d - very cold am; dry winter h - hot and dry most of the year k - cold and dry most of the year. This is how these letters are assigned to climatic belts e.g polar and sub-polar (sub arctic) regions begin with the letter E, to which are added either T (for tundra vegetation and conditions). The dry climates are assigned the letter W and S to differentiate between desert (BW) and steppe (BS) climate and vegetation conditions. BWK would refer to cool desert climate while DFe would refer to cold snowy forest climate with cool short summer.

waec-geography-theory-0081.explanation: (a) The characteristics of the tropical grass land vegetation include: (i) Dry season lasts for 6-7 months (ii) Tall trees reaching 2m dominate the vegetation (iii) Scattered trees mainly in the river valley called savanna parkland (iv) Around the equator the trees are bigger and more common than grasses called savanna woodland (v) Towards the desert with less rainfall there are few trees with short grasses called savanna scrub. Some of the trees here e.g acacia, baobab, etc are deciducus (i.e shod the it leaves during the dry season) (b) The economic values of this vegetation type to the inhabitants of the region include: (i) Livestock farming (e.g cattle rearing) is the most important occupation E.g Hausa - Fulani cattle rearers, Massai of Kenya etc. are known to be heavily involved in livestock farming. (ii) Grain cultivation: Some elements 3f grains such as millets, sorghum and maize are widely cultivated. Groundnut and cotton can also be cultivated (ii:) Game reserves. Most of these grasslands serve as game reserves e.g National Park of South Africa and Yankari Same Reserves are centres of attraction for tourism.

waec-geography-theory-0082.explanation: (a) Two main types of environmental pollution are: (i) Air pollution (ii) water pollution Three causes of water pollution include: (I) The release of disease-producing (pathogenic) bacteria and viruses (biological pollution diseases (ii) Undesirable ions and compounds in solution (chemical pollution) into water thereby changing its colour, taste and/or smell (iii) Oil spillage - the bursting of oil pipes results in oil spillage into water thereby changing the colour, taste and smell of the water. (b) Three effects of pollution on man are: (i) Atmospheric pollution, which may be caused by fog reduces visibility. This poses a serious danger to motorists and pilots (ii) Pollutants may have adverse psychological effects on man and animals e.g discomfort, chronic diseases, such as lung cancer and asthma, impairment of growth and death (iii) Some pollutants are toxic and can kill plants e.g sulfur dioxide and hydrogen fluoride are toxic to plants from which man gets his food.

waec-geography-theory-0083.explanation: (a) Two physical factors which may attract or favour a rapid growth of population are: (i) Favourable climate: This leads to dense population, e.g temperate regions like U.K. U.S.A Japan tend to have increased population because of good climate (ii) Fertile soils. Fertile soils attract population, e.g fertile alluvial soil in the deltas of South East Asia, River Nile in Egypt have attracted dense population. Two human factors which may favour a rapid growth of population are: (i) Commercial activities, Commercial activities like heavy trading centres, and presence of ports are closely associated with population concentration (ii) Mining activities. Mining activities in areas where minerals are available tend to attract high concentration of people. (b) Five problems that may arise from rapid growth of population include: (i) Accommodation problem (ii) Transportation problem (iii) High pressure on existing social amenities (iv) High level of crimes (v) Traffic congestion

waec-geography-theory-0084.explanation: (a) Three types of rural settlements are: (i) Isolated settlement - One or a few houses only are found in a remote area (ii) Two or more houses without shops, schools, or services also in remote area (iii) Village - Many houses where several hundreds or thousands of people are found usually with small shops and limited services (b) Four ways in which rural and urban settlements are interdependent: (i) Rural settlements are sources of food for urban settlements (i) Urban settlements are usually the sources of manufactured goods for the rural areas (iii) Urban settlements are the sources of jobs or educational opportunities for the rural settlements (iv) Urban settlements may also serve as administrative headquarters of the rural settlements

waec-geography-theory-0085.explanation: The contribution of transportation to the economic development of Nigeria (i) It makes available to a community goods produced elsewhere (ii) Transportation makes for regional specialisation in production. If goods are not moved, each region will produce less (iii) Development of large cities depends on cheap and efficient transport system (iv) It reduces the cost of goods to the consumers (v) It reduces waste from over-production and stabilizes prices (vi) it strengthens national unity as people from different parts of Nigeria easily interact with one another (vii) It helps in national defense as troops can easily be moved to places where they are needed.

waec-geography-theory-0086.explanation: (a) Government influences on the location of industries in tropical Africa. Government can directly or indirectly influence the location of industries. Such government influence may be owing to political, social, economic or military reasons. Government influences the location indirectly by offering incentives such as tax reliefs or low land rent, provision of basic amenities for the establishment of industries in an area. (b) Nearness to market as a factor of industries location in Tropical Africa. Market is one of the factors affecting the location of industries. Industry will not be located where there is no market. Industries are located in areas of high population density because of the high purchasing power of the urban dwellers. Cost of transportation of manufactured goods is also reduced, and those industries whose finished products are bulkier than the raw materials are usually located at or near the market, e.g soft drinks and beer industries whose products are not only bulky but also breakable are located on or near the market. (c) Concentration of manufacturing industries in urban centres of developing countries is due to (i) Proximity to power, e.g electricity is easily available in urban areas (ii) Supply of labour - due to high population in urban area, cheap labour can easily be available for the industries to use (iii) Reduction in cost of transportation. Since there are good road network coupled with numerous vehicles, cost of transportation of both raw material and finished goods is reduced (iv) Favourable market. Urban areas serve as good market for the location of industries because of high purchasing power of the urban dwellers (iv) Easy source of capital: Most urban areas provide the means, i.e banks where entrepreneurs can easily get loan to boost their production

waec-geography-theory-0087.explanation: Five factors that determine the volume of trade between Nigeria and Ghana include: (i) If the goods produced by both countries are not similar. If they are not similar, the volume of trade will increase, but if they are similar the volume of trade is going to be reduced. (ii) Differences in climatic conditions: If there are differences in climatic conditions necessary for the production of certain crops, both countries will specialise in the production of different crops which will eventually lead to exchange of goods but if the climatic conditions are the same, both will specialise in the production of the same crops (iii) The degree of industrial development: If one of the countries develops more industrially than the other, one will definitely demand for more manufactured goods than the other, hence exchange of goods (international trade) (iv) Prices of goods offered: It the prices of goods offered by one of the countries is higher than what other countries may offer, the volume of trade will be increased but if the prices are low, one will expect a low volume of trade (v) Foreign exchange earnings: If the foreign exchange earnings from both countries are high, then the volume of trade will increase but if the earnings are low the volume of trade will also be low

waec-geography-theory-0088.explanation: (b) Four ways in which the forest vegetation contributes to the economy of the country are: (i) Provision of timber for construction of houses and furniture (ii) Provision of foreign exchange earnings from the export of timber (iii) Forest vegetation provides jobs to many people, e.g forest guards, lumbermen (iv) Forest vegetation also provides medicinal herbs for the pharmaceutical industries. (c) Four problems associated with exploitation of forest vegetation include: (i) Heterogeneous nature of trees (ii) Lack of motorable roads (iii) High cost of survey to determine economic trees (iv) Felling of timber is risky as many people have lost their lives in the process

waec-geography-theory-0089.explanation: (a) Hinterland refers to the area of land that can be served by a particular sea port (b) The importance of sea ports in the economy of Nigeria include: (i) Sea ports like Apapa port serves as a point where imported and exported goods come in or move out of the country respectively (ii) Sea ports generally like Port Harcourt and Apapa ports generate , revenue for the government (iii) Sea ports generally provide employment for many people (iv) Sea ports bring people together for the exchange of ideas and culture (c) Four problems of port development in Nigeria are: (i) The Deposition of sand, silt, clay at the delta and along the coast makes port development a problem (ii) The nature of the coastline poses a problem as most coastlines are not suited for the development of ports (iii) Shallow nature of the coasts; Most of the coasts in Nigeria are very shallow and this makes it difficult for large vessels to sail to the coast (iv) Fluctuations in ocean tides: There is fluctuation in tides (rise in the volume of water in the ocean) along the coasts as there are occasions of high tides and other occasions of low tide Sokoto Plain

waec-geography-theory-0090.explanation: Sokoto plain Eastern highlands (a) Relief and drainage The relief is a lowland of less than 30m. Broken up by rivers Sokoto and Rima and their tributaries and their areas is usually flooded during the rainy season There are chains of hills along eastern border of Nigeria e.g Mambila, Biu Plateaux, Alantika, Shebshi mountains, Adamawa plateau. They range in altitude between 600m and 200m. The rivers that flow within this zone are Benue, Gongola, Taraba, kano, etc. (b) Resources and human activities Minerals found are limestone, gold, phosphate and gypsum. They are also involved in farming and rearing of cattle, sheep and goat, Industries are cement and local crafts Presence of minerals like limestone, iron ore and uranium. They are involved in agriculture, e.g cultivation of tea, coffee, yam, cassava, cattle, goat, sheep, etc and few industries like cement and textile. (c) Problems of development (i) Inadequate supply of rainfall (ii) Desert encroachment due to activities of man (ii) Extensive land make communication very difficult (i) Rugged relief causes remoteness and poor development of transportation (ii) Problem of soil erosion and severe flooding (iii) Cimatic variation due'to rainfall in some areas and none in other areas

waec-geography-theory-0091.explanation: (b) Three problems which result from the concentration of manufacturing industries in these zones are: (i) Industrial and air pollution (ii) Competition resulting in lower prices of goods (iii) High pressure on existing social amenities like electricity, water, etc (c) Three steps that can be taken to encourage the growth of industries outside these zones are: (i) Provision of electricity, water, healthcare outside these zones (ii) Granting of loans to entrepreneurs who want to build industries outside these zones (iii) Granting of free land and long tax holiday to industries sited outside these zones.

waec-geography-theory-0092.explanation: (a) Cocoa growing in Western Nigeria: Cocoa is cultivated in the Western Nigeria especially in Oyo, Ogun and Ondo States because cocoa grows best under certain conditions present in these areas which are undulating and well drained land, temperature of about 27°C, rainfall of 125-200cm, abundant sunshine for drying the beans, abundant labour to work in the cocoa farm and easy disposal of produce through sea ports. Crops sowed mature within five years. Harvested pods are crushed,beans fermented, dried and bagged for export. (b) Oil palm production in the Eastern States: Oil palm is produced in the east like Owerri, Aba, Port Harcourt, etc. The crop grows best in temperature of not less than 21°C rainfall of 150-300cm, brilliant sunshine, deep loamy soil coupled with abundance of cheap labour. The crop is grown from the nuts, matures within 5-10 years and the matured fruits or bunch are harvested; processed and the products are palm oil and palm kernel which are used locally or exported. (c) Rice cultivation in the Middle Belt: Rice is cultivated mainly as food crop for internal trade. Swamp rice is the type that is mainly grown in the middle belt of Nigeria such as Lafiagi, Badeggi and Pategi areas of the Niger valley. The seeds, are first raised in nursery and later transplanted to the Niger valley where the Niger has flooded its valley. They rice grows between 3-4 months after which it is harvested, processed and sold to local buyers. (d) Intensive Farming in the Kano close - settled Zone; Intensive farming is practised in Kano as a result of high population. This high population results in land fragmentation hence farmers have to maximise the use of the small land through farming. During the farming seasons, they apply fertilizers and manure to promote the growth of crops and most of the crops grown are mainly cereals e.g millet, sorghum, maize

waec-geography-theory-0093.explanation: (b) Three reasons for the length of rainy season in the area having less than four months or rain annually. (i) Long distance from the ocean. The area is too far from the ocean (ii) Nearness to the desert. The area is very close to the sahara desert, hence it experiences low rainfall. (iii) Effects of trade winds. The N. E trade winds tend to have more influence on the area than the S.E trade winds. (c) Three problems due tc continuous rainfall all the year round are: (i) Soil erosion: Too much rain results in soil erosion (ii) Leaching: Too much rain leads to loss of nutrients from the surface of the soil (iii) Poor yield of crops due to either damage to the crop or lack of sufficient sunshine to produce fruits.

waec-geography-theory-0094.explanation: (b) Six benefits Liberia derives from its membership of the ECOWAS: (i) There has been increase in trade between Liberia and other ECOWAS members (ii) Liberia was once involved in civil war but is now a peaceful country through the effort of ECOMOG (iii) Free movement of Liberians within the sub-region has fostered unity and cooperation between Liberia and others (iv) Road development between Liberia and her neighbours has helped in the transport network of Liberia (v) Border dispute between Liberia and Sierra Leone has been settled by ECOWAS members (vi) Liberia's participation in ECOWAS games held in Lagos in 1977 aided understanding and solidarity among the states.

waec-geography-theory-0095.explanation: (b) One method of mining petroleum is drilling: (i) The underground rocks are sampled and tested for traces of oil (ii) When oil is discovered, a well is sunk to reach it by the help of a drilling rig or derrick (iii) The oil is then pumped out (iv) A system of valves called "Christmas tree" is created to control the flow into tanks (c) Four problems associated with mining in West Africa; (i) Lack of fund (ii) Lack of technical know-how (iii) Absence of minerals (iv) Lack of sources of efficient and reliable power

waec-geography-theory-0096.explanation: (b) Four importance of rivers to Africa; (i) Generation of hydro-electric power (H.E.P) (ii) For fishing (iii) For irrigation of farmlands (iv)As means of transportation (inland navigation)

waec-geography-theory-0097.explanation: (a) Economic importance of Aswan High Dam to the Nile Basin are: (i) Generation of Hydro-electric power (electricity) (ii) Aswan dam also serves irrigation purposes. This enables the people to farm throughout the year (iii) Dam is also used as fishing ground (iv) Aswan dam also provides source of water for domestic and industrial uses (v) Aswan dam also serves as tourist centre where revenue can be generated. (b) Four problems resulting from the construction of dams are: (i) There may be low level of water in the river which may hamper navigation and other activities (ii) The collapse of the dam may lead to flooding of the plain which may cause damage to life and properties (iii) Huge amount of money which would have been utilized in some useful projects is lost through the construction of dam (iv) Shortage of water in the river during dry season may hamper the normal functioning of the dam.

waec-geography-theory-0098.explanation: (a) (i) Equinoxes: Refers to two particular days of the year when all parts of the world will experience equal days and nights. These two days are March 21st and September 23rd. During these two days, the sun is vertically overhead at the equator and all parts of the earth will experience equal days and equal nights. (ii) Great Circles: Any circle which divides a globe into two equal parts (or hemispheres) is a great circle. Examples are the equator, Greenwich meridian, meridian 180°, meridians 10°E and 170°W. 50°E and 130°W. etc. are all great circles. The number of great circles is limitless. It can extend east to west, north to south and so on provided it divides the globe into hemispheres. (b) The reason(s) why the period of twilight is longer along the Arctic circle than at the Equator; The brief period between sun set and complete darkness is called twilight. This is caused by the fact that during the period of twilight, the earth receives diffused or refracted light from the sun while it is still below the horizon. Since the sunrises and sets in a vertical path at the Equator, the period during which refracted light is received is short. But at the arctic circle, the sun rises and sets in an obligue path and the period of refracted light is longer. It is much longer still at the poles.

waec-geography-theory-0099.explanation: (a) The differences between deflation and abrasion are as follows; Deflation involves the lifting and blowing away of loose materials from the ground. Such unconsolidated sands and pebbles may be carried in the air or rolled along the ground depending on the size while abrasion involves the sand blasting of rock surfaces by winds when they hurl sand particles against them. The effect of sand blasting results in rock surfaces being scratched, polished and worn away. (b) One landform produced by deflation is the deflation hollows. Deflation results in the lowering of the land surface gradually until large depressions are formed called deflation hollows. One landform produced by abrasion is the Rock pedestals. The sand blasting effect of winds against any projecting rock masses wears back the soft layers so that an irregular edge is formed on the alternate bands of hard and soft rocks. Grooves and hollows are cut in the rock surfaces, carving them into fantastic pillars called rock pedestals. (c) Two reasons why wind erosion is more active in arid than in humid regions. (i) In arid regions like the desert, wind erosion is more active because of absence of vegetation. Absence of vegetation enables the-wind to move at high speed thereby causing wind erosion. (ii) Absence of moisture to bind the soil particles together. Since there is no moisture, the soil particles are loosely held hence they can easily be carried away by winds.

waec-geography-theory-0100.explanation: (a) (i) Three of Koppen's major climatic groups ere: (i) Those based on climate and vegetation (ii) Those based on temperature (iii) Those based on precipitation-evaporation ratios. (ii) The basis of Koppen's classification is vegetation. (b) Two types of climate within Koppen's first group and their features are: (i) The moist and Hot climate; features; (i) Tropical rainy climate (ii) Average monthly temperature above 18°C (iii) Climate has no winter seasons (iv) Annual rainfall is large and exceeds annual evaporation (ii) The moist and warm climate: features: (i) Coldest month has an average temperature of under 18°C (ii) Has above —3°C in at least one month (iii) Has an average temperature of above 10°C (iv) It has both summer and winter seasons.

waec-geography-theory-0101.explanation: Two of the vegetation types are; (a) Equatorial (b) Tropical desert (i) Characteristics of Equatorial vegetation are: (i) The trees are evergreen due to absence of dry season. (ii) The trees are mainly tall and broad leafed (iii) The trees are mainly tropical hardwood (iv) Trees are heterogeneous (different species) (v) There are three distinct layers of the forest upper, middle and lower storeys (vi) Lots of undergrowth e.g climbers, epiphytes, ropes, etc (ii) The climatic conditions which influence the vegetation are: (i) Great uniformity of temperatures throughout the year (ii) The annual range of temperature is not more than 30°C (iii) High mean monthly temperature, which is always around 26°C (iv) Very heavy rainfall of 150 — 200cm, per annum which is well distributed. (i) Characteristics of tropical desert are: (i) Presence of combination of plants — grass, shrubs, herbs, roots etc. (ii) Presence of xerophytes (drought resistant shrubs) e.g bulbous cacti (iii) Presence of halophytes (salt loving plants) (iv) Plants possess long roots with little or no leaves (v) some possess thick succulent stems. (vi) some shed their leaves during dry season (ii) How the vegetation is influenced by climate; (i) Temperature is very high (30°C - 58°C) (ii) Mean annual temperature is 32°C (iii) Annual range of temperature is 9°C. (iv) Rainfall is very low (25cm per annum)

waec-geography-theory-0102.explanation: (a) Causes of urban flooding: (i) Abundant supply of water from rainfall or ice (ii) High water table which ensures a steady water supply (iii) Weak dam construction and embarkments (iv) Poor drainage system (v) Blocking of drainage systems e.g gutters (vi) Unplanned urban settlements (b) Effects of urban flooding: (i) Human lives are lost during urban flooding (ii) Properties are damaged (iii) Some roads may be washed away or rendered impassable (iv) Some houses are completely taken over by water during flooding (v) Deposits of garbage left behind by flood can cause environmental pollution. (c) Control measure of urban flooding: (i) Construction of strong embankments along the banks of rivers (ii) Retardation of run off over the surface of water sheds (iii) Storage of flood water behind dams to serve as flood control reservoirs (iv) Stream channelization (v) Legislation against indiscrimate dumping of refuse in gutters. (vi).Construction of functional drainage systems.

waec-geography-theory-0103.explanation: (a)(i) Latitude is the angular distance of a point on the Earth's surface, measured in degrees from the centre of the earth. Lines of Latitude run from West to East and they can be used to calculate distance between one place to another. It extends between 90°N and 90°S. Longitudes are imaginery lines running from the North to the South at right angle to the parallel. The longitude that passes through the centre of the earth is called the prime or Greenwich Meridian. Longitude can be used to calculate local time and it extends between 180°W and 180°E. (ii) Standard Time; is the time generally adopted by a particular country which is usually taken from the central meridian of that country. The need is to eliminate difference in local time between one town and another; otherwise it will result in changing time from one town to another. E.g Nigeria has accepted the meridian of 15°E for her standard time which is 1 hour ahead of the Greenwich Mean Time: Greenwich Mean Time is the time along the prime or Greenwich Meridian which is longitude 0°. It is from the GMT that all countries take their time E.g London and Accra are on longitude 0° and all other countries take their time from the GMT from London. If the GMT in London is 3.00pm, Nigerian time will be 4.00pm. (ii) Find the time difference The time difference from 10.00am 5th July to 4.48am 4th July = 29 hours 12 mins. 29 hours 12 mins - 24 hours (one day) = 5hrs 12 minutes (iii) Convert time difference (5 hrs 12 minutes)to longitude 15° = 1 hour 5 hrs = 15° x 5 =75° 4 minutes = 1° 12 mins. 12 = 3° 4 Total degree = 75° + 3° = 78° (iv) Since X° is west of 0°, the longitude therefore is 78°W

waec-geography-theory-0104.explanation: (a) Sedimentary rock is the type of rock formed from the accumulation of layers of deposits of sediments in water or on land. These sediments later join or cement together in layers to form sedimentary rock. Two processes of sedimentary rock formation are: (i) Mechanical Process: Involves the formation of sedimentary rock from sediments accumulated from other rocks such as igneous and metamorphic rocks. These rocks settled in layers to form sedimentary rock E., J, formation of sandstone, shale, conglomerate. (ii) Chemical Process: Pre-existing igneous and metamorphic rocks are precipitated chemically from solution of one kind or the other. Rock salt are derived from strata which once formed the beds of seas or lakes. Examples of rocks formed by chemical process include sodium chloride, gypsum, etc. (b) Three ways in which sedimentary rocks are important to man are: (i) Some sedimentary rocks are sources of some useful minerals such as coal and petroleum which serve as fuel energy to man. (ii) Some sedimentary rocks are used for road construction and for building houses. (iii) Rock salt, e.g sodium chloride (table salt) is a source of body mineral needed for maintaining osmotic pressure in the blood.

waec-geography-theory-0105.explanation: Four factors which determine the direction of flow of ocean current are (i) Planetary winds (ii) Temperature (iii) Salinity (iv) The Earth's rotation (i) Planetary Winds: Between the equator and the tropics, the Trade Winds move equatorial water polewards and westwards and warm the eastern coasts of continents, e.g the North - East Trade winds move the North Equatorial current, Florida current and Gulf stream Drift, to warm the Southern and Eastern coasts of U.S.A. (ii) Temperature: Because of the difference in temperature of ocean waters at the equator and at the poles the warm water is,lighter and rises and the cold water is denser and sinks hence warm equatorial water moves slowly along the surface poleward and the cold water moves equatorwards. (iii) Salinity: Water of high salinity are denser than water of low salinity hence water of low salinity flows on the surface of water of high salinity (iv) Rotation of the earth: The earth rotates from west to east and causes the ocean water to deflect to the right thereby making ocean water to deflect in a clockwise direction in the Northern hemisphere and anticlockwise in the Southern hemisphere. (b) Effects of ocean current on the climate of the adjacent coastal areas, (i) Warm current raise the temperatures of adjacent lands (ii) Warm current brings regular and heavy rainfall to the coastlands (iii) Warm current helps to keep ports in polar region free from ice (iv) Cold current causes aridity and desert e.g Benguela current of west coast of South Africa causes Namid desert (v) The meeting of two different current (i.e cold and warm currents) is a blessing as it results in the growth of planktons where fishing can be done.

waec-geography-theory-0106.explanation: (b) The type of climate represented by the data is the Tropical Continental (Sudan type) climate (c) Four reasons for the answer in (b) are (i) The annual range for the temperature is 10°C (ii) Rainy season begins in May and lasts till September and the rest of the year is cool and dry (iii) It has one single maximum of rainfall which is August (iv) The annual mean temperature is 27°C.

waec-geography-theory-0108.explanation: (a) Environmental resource is any resource within our environment which is useful to man (b) The importance of water as an environmental resource include the following: (i) Rain water enables our crops to grow (ii) Water from rivers can be used for construction of hydro-electric power supply (H. E. P) (iii) Rainwater and water from rivers can be used for domestic and industrial uses (iv) Rivers and seas provide employment for many people e.g fishermen (v) Rivers, ponds, lakes, oceans provide food in form of protein to man e.g fish, shrimps crabs, etc (vi) Rivers and ocean can be used for tourist centres (c) Three sources of water: (i) Rain water (ii) Water from rivers (iii) Water from the ground (ponds or wells)

waec-geography-theory-0109.explanation: (a) Four functions of towns include: (i) Industrial function (ii) Commercial function (iii) Administrative function (iv) Residential function (b) Four ways the initial function of a town contribute to its growth: (i) As a result of the siting of many industries in a town due to large market, easy transportation, availability of power; people tend to migrate to the town to take up employment in the industries (ii) Also, as a result of commercial activities in the town, people tend to settle in the town resulting in the growth of that town. (iii) Due to the fact that the seat of government is located there, people tend to move closer to the government resulting in the growth of the town (iv) The availability of social amenities such as pipe-borne water, electricity, etc, people tend to move into the town to enjoy these amenities resulting in its growth. (c) Three ways in which rural settlements are dependent on urban settlements include: (i) Urban settlements are usually the sources of manufactured goods for the rural settlements. (ii) Urban settlements may also serve as administrative headquarters of the rural settlements (iii) It is also a source of employment to rural settlements

waec-geography-theory-0110.explanation: Ways in which poor transportation can limit the economic development of a country e.g Niger Republic include: (i) Poor transportation hinders easy movement of goods from one part of the country to another (ii) It tends to reduce specialisation in production because there are no ways produce can easily move out or come into the country (iii) Poor transportation lowers economic development because of lack of linkages of areas of production with consumption centres (iv) It reduces trade between towns and countries (v) It also lowers international integration and peace (vi) Poor transportation hinders diffusion of ideas and innovations.

waec-geography-theory-0111.explanation: (a) Reasons for the relatively low level of industrial development in tropical Africa are: (i) Inadequate capital. Entrepreneurs in Africa do not have large capital to establish industries (ii) Inadequate skilled manpower. There is serious shortage of skilled labour especially in management and technical staff (iii) Small market The existence of small market (i.e consumers) prevents the growth of industries in Africa (iv) Inadequate infrastructure -electricity, pipe borne water, telecommunication, roads, etc, are lacking hence a low growth of industries in Africa (v) Shortage of raw-materials - Raw materials are not adequately available locally hence some depend on imported raw materials. This lowers industrial growth. (b) Five contributions of industrial sector to the economic development of the region include: (i) It leads to the diversification of economies (ii) It has helped to conserve foreign exchange that would have been used in the importation of goods (iii) Industrial sector provides employment to many people (iv) It also raises the general standard of living of the people (v) Industrial goods exported also generate foreign exchange to the country.

waec-geography-theory-0112.explanation: (a)(i) One sea route that links Nigeria with Europe is the Cape route (ii) Two countries in Europe that trade with Nigeria using this route are Britain and Germany (b) Four products carried along the route are: (i) Petroleum (ii) Cocoa (iii) Electronics (iv) Oil palm (c) Five ways in which international trade is important to Nigeria include; (i) Generation of foreign exchange from exportation (ii) It has helped in specialisation in the production of certain crops, e.g oil palm, cocoa, etc (iii) Goods that are not manufactured in Nigeria are imported into the country (iv) Exchange of personnel who possess the technical know-how and expertise in production of goods and services (v) It has promoted international cooperation and peace.

waec-geography-theory-0113.explanation: (a) (i) Rainfall has a lot of effects on agricultural activities in the tropical continental region of Nigeria in the following ways: (i) Rainfall is low in this region (ii) As a result of low rainfall, it gives rise to savanna type of vegetation (iii) Agricultural activities in this area include the cultivation of cereal crops like maize, rice, millet sorghum, etc. (iv) It also results in the rearing of cattle, sheep and cat due to abundance of grasses (v) Low rainfall prevents the spread of tsetse flies thereby promoting the livestock activities (ii) on sub-equatorial region of Nigeria (i) Rainfall is very high in the sub-equatorial region of Nigeria (ii) This high rainfall gives rise to rainforest type of vegetation (iii) Agricultural activities in this re igo n involve the growth of tree crops like cocoa, kola, oil palm, rubber, etc (iv) Due to lack of grasses, livestock is not popular. (v) Timber is present hence people involve in lumbering activities. (b) Five contributions of agriculture to the economy of Nigeria include: (i) Provision of food for the people (ii) It provides raw materials for industries (iii) It provides employment to many people (iv) It generates foreign exchange for the country (v) It leads to the development of towns and villages

waec-geography-theory-0114.explanation: (b) Four problems facing river transportation in Nigeria are: (i) Shallowness of some rivers especially during the dry seasons (ii) Presence of rapids and cataracts prevents navigation (iii) Most rivers do not flow to the desired places which are of economic importance (iv) Most rivers pass through thick vegetation and the debris formed from falling leaves and trees makes navigation difficult. (c) These problems can be solved through: (i) Dredging some parts of navigable rivers (ii) Removal of cataracts (iii) Cutting down of close trees to rivers

waec-geography-theory-0115.explanation: (b)(i) Three advantages of low population density in Minna include: (i) Absence of environmental pollution (ii) Availability of comfortable accommodation (iii) Absence of traffic congestion (ii)Three advantages of high population density in Lagos. (i) Availability of employment (ii) Presence of heavy commercial activities (iii) Presence of social amenities

waec-geography-theory-0116.explanation: (a)(i) Two local craft industries are: (i) Leather work in Kano and Sokoto (ii) Fibre industries in Kaduna and Ibadan (ii) Two manufacturing industries are: (i) Cement industries in Ewekoro and Nkalagu (ii) Oil refineries in Warri and Port Harcourt (b) Four problems facing local industries in Nigeria include: (i) Inadequate capital (ii) The use of simple and local tools (iii) They lack international patronage (iv) They lack the technical know-how of the craft. (c) Three ways the problems are being solved: (i) Provision of loans to prospective craftsmen (ii) Provision of modern equipment to boost production (iii) Training people to acquire more technical skills

waec-geography-theory-0117.explanation: (b)(i) Four physical features of the Niger Delta are: (i) Climate is hot and wet characterized by heavy rainfall and high temperatures (ii) It has a dense and luxuriant mangrove swamp forest (iii) Niger delta is purely a lowland area (iv) The place is entirely swampy (ii) Four physical features of the North- Central Plateau are: (i) The relief is dominated by the highland of Hausa land with flat summits (ii) It is the widest, well-drained region in Nigeria giving rise to many rivers (iii) Climate is continental with low rainfall and moderate temperature (iv) The vegetation is purely the Sudan type with abundance of grasses.

waec-geography-theory-0118.explanation: (b) There is direct relationship between pressure belts and rainfall distribution in Vest Africa. Pressure belts are created by temperature. When the temperature of a place is very high, it creates a high pressure belt. Wind which carries a lot of moisture therefore blows from a region of high pressure belt to regions of low pressure belts. This therefore results in heavy rainfall in areas of low pressure belts and light rainfall in areas of high pressure belts.

waec-geography-theory-0119.explanation: (b) Three ways in which climate affects dams in West Africa include: (i) High rainfall increases the volume of water in the rivers while low rainfall lowers the amount of rainfall in rivers (ii) High temperature tends to evaporate water from dams (iii) Period of seasons, long dry season tends to reduce the volume of water in the rivers. (c) Three advantages of dams to West Africa are: (i) Generation of Hydro-Electric Power (H.E.P) (ii) For irrigation purposes (iii) It improves fishing and water navigation. Three disadvantages of dams to West Africa are: (i) Shortage of water in dam disrupts H.E.P output (ii) It leads to low volume of water in rivers which hinders river navigation (iii) Collapse of dams can result in urban flooding destroying properties and killing people.

waec-geography-theory-0120.explanation: (b) Four ways in which relief of Africa poses problems to the construction of trans-African highway from Cape of Good Hope to Cairo are: (i) Presence of many highlands such as Kilimanjaro, Kenya highlands, etc. (ii) Presence of many rivers which will demand high cost of constructing bridges across the rivers (iii) Presence of deep valleys e.g Great East rift valley (iv) Effects of wind erosion and deposition can disrupt the construction of such road. (c) These problems can be minimized by; (i) Construction of roads on fairly lowland areas (ii)Avoiding presence of high mountains and valleys (iii)Avoiding the presence of big rivers and planting trees along the roads in desert area.
