waec-geography-theory-0123.explanation: (a) Four ways in which lines of latitude differ from lines of longitude Lines of latitude Lines of longitude (i) Lines of latitude run from west to east (ii) Lines of latitude are used to calculate distance between one place and another (iii) Lines of latitude cannot be used to calculate local time (iv) Latitude extent on the globe is 90°S to 90°N - Lines of longitude run from north to south - Lines of longitude cannot be used to calculate distances between one place and another - Lines of longitude are used in calculating local time - Longitudinal extent on the globe is from 180°E to 180°W (iv) Time and date are 5.00pm + 13 hours = 6.00pm The following day which is Satudary Answer = 6.00a.m Saturday

waec-geography-theory-0124.explanation: Characteristics and mode of formation of block mountain. Block mountain is formed from faulting and it involves the following: (i) Two parallel faults develop (ii) The block enclosed by the two parallel faults remains as it is (iii) The land on either side of the parallel faults subsides (iv) The enclosed centre-block, now up standing becomes the horst or block mountain (b) Characteristics and mode of formation of Zengen: Zengen is formed as a result of wind abrasion. ​​​​​Zengens are formed in areas in the desert which have a surface layer to hard rock over-lying another layer of soft rock. Before wind abrasion can produce Zengen, fissures or cracks opened by very high temperature on the desert surface must have occurred on the hard surface layer. Wind abrasion then attacks the desert surface through the fissures already existing. The fissures are widened to become furrows while the blocks between the fissures (now furrows) become ridges called "Zengens"

waec-geography-theory-0125.explanation: Features Equatorial climate Tundra Climate (i) Climatic zones and latitude (ii) Animal rainfall (iii) Period of maximum rainfall (iv) Type of rainfall (v) Mean annual temperature (vi)Annual range of temperature (vii) Example of country located in the zone - Equatorial Climate Equatorial - - - zone and 0 - 10°N - Average of 250cm - All year round with double maxima July and September - Convectional - 27°C - 2°C - 3°C - Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia - Cold zone and 65 - 90°N - Average 25cm - Rainfall is irregular, more rainfall winter - Cyclonic - 8.3°C - 27°C - Upernavik in Greenland

waec-geography-theory-0126.explanation: (a) Soil is defined as the uppermost layer of the earth crust in which plants get supports and food (or nutrient. (b) The process of soil formation is called weathering. Weathering is defined as the breaking down of rocks into tir pieces to form soil (c) The process of weathering involves three processes: (i) Physical weathering (ii) Chemical weathering (iii) Biological weathering (i) Physical Weathering: This involves the breaking down of rocks into tin pieces by special agents such as temperature, running water, ice,wind, pressure, etc. (ii) Chemical Weathering; This involves the breaking down of rocks into tiny pieces by chemical means such as solution, oxidation, carbonation hydrolysis and hydration. (iii) Biological weathering: Involves the breaking down of rocks by biological agent suc as earthworm, roots of plants, hooves of animals, rodents and the activities of man. (c) Soil Profile: A vertical section cut across the soil to show the arrangement of layers is called soil profile. The different horizontal layers are called horizons and there are 3 main horizons in a well-weathered soil namely. A - horizon B - horizon and C - horizon. A Horizon: This is the top soil. It contains remains of plants and anima which have decomposed to form humus, it is also known as the alluvial horizon which is derived by the washing c clay and fine soil particles down the soil profile. B - Horizon: This is zone of enrichment (alluvial horizon or accumulatic of soil minerals). The minerals have been washed down from the A- horizon and converted into inorganic compound It is regarded as the sub-soil C - Horizon: This is the layer of underlying weathered debris. It is the source of pares material. It in underlain by hard unweathered rock.

waec-geography-theory-0127.explanation: (a) Four components of the ecosystem are: (i) Lithosphere (solid-earth crust) (ii) Hydrosphere (liquid component) (iii)Atmosphere (gaseous component) (iv) Biosphere (Living organisms component). (b) Carbon cycles have helped to explain the inter-dependence of the components in the ecosystem in the following ways. (i) There is the inter-relationship between plants and the atmosphere as it is from the atmosphere that plan. derive the carbon dioxide that they need for photosynthesis. Then man and other animals give out carbon dioxide through the process of respiration. (ii) There is an inter-dependence within the biotic components themselves. The herbivores together with the carnivores and decomposers, pass on the energy and matter (iii) Man also contribute to the carbon in the atmosphere through the burning of fossil fuel, e.g coal, petroleum, liquid gas and burning of wood

waec-geography-theory-0128.explanation: (a) Reasons for rapid-growth of world population in the last two decades are: (i) Modernization of agriculture leading to plentiful and varied food supply (ii) Improved health services (iii) Knowledge of the cause of infectious diseases and how to prevent them (iv) Better sanitation (v) Reduced infant mortality rate as a result of better care (vi) A lowering of the marriage age from 22 to 20 and below (vii) Change in child bearing pattern as women want to have all their children at once and have a rest later (viii) Modernization and industrialization make standard of living to improve. (b) Three problems arising from this rapid growth; (i) Problem of housing (accommodation) (ii) Problem of transportation (iii) Shortage of food (or starvation) (c) Solutions to these problems; (i) Government and other agencies should establish residential estates (ii) More roads, railways and other transportation network to take care of the increasing population (iii) Mechanized agriculture should be practised.

waec-geography-theory-0129.explanation: (a) Urban settlement is a relatively large, dense and permanent settlement of socially heterogeneous individuals usually found in towns, cities or megalopolis while rural settlement is a relatively small and scattered settlement of socially and culturally homogenous individuals found in villages or hamlets. (b) Four factors responsible for the increase in size of urban settlement include: (i) Availability of jobs (or employments) (ii) Presence of social amenities, e.g electricity, water (iii) Presence of administrative headquarters in urban area (iv) Involvement of people in commercial and industrial activities in urban areas (c) Four problems associated with urban growth: (i) Inadequate transport facilities (ii) Undue increase in human and vehicular traffic (iii) Overuse and deterioration of available social services (iv) increase in the rate of crimes.

waec-geography-theory-0130.explanation: (a) Four ways in which physical factors may hinder the development of road transportation are: (i) Rugged highlands create pattern for the development of roads (ii) Climatic factors like rainfall can wash away existing roads or make it more difficult to construct new ones (iii) Rivers, especially large ones do contribute greatly to the development of roads as huge amount is spent in the construction and erection of bridges (iv) Swampy area is also a problem as it also takes large amount of money to construct bridges and flyovers across them. (b) Four factors responsible for the poor network of railways in tropical African countries include: (i) Capital costs for maintenance and operation of rail transport are usually high (ii) Lack of spare parts and technical know-how tend to reduce the rail transportation (iii) Rail lines are constructed only around mineral or agricultural producing areas hence the absence of these products results in low development of rail (iv) it is relatively too slow and people do not want to travel with it.

waec-geography-theory-0131.explanation: (a) Three differences between light industries and heavy industries Light industries Heavy industries (i) They produce relatively small light weight goods, e.g shoes (ii)-The products of light industries are mainly final or consumer goods (iii) It usually employs a lot of female workers (i) They produce heavy and bulky goods, e,g iron and steel (ii) Products are not final nor consumer good rather they are used in construction or manufacturing industries (iii) It employs male workers due to the nature of work involved (b) Four reasons why light industries are more prevalent than heavy industries in tropical Africa are: (i) Lack of capital; Poor funding leads to the establishment of light industries than heavy industries (ii) Lack of technical know-how: Africans do not have the skills for heavy industrial operations (iii) Lack of raw materials; Raw materials: for heavy, industries are lacking in African countries (iv) Africans generally tend to engage in production of consumable goo than non-consumable goods because of the low level of development.

waec-geography-theory-0132.explanation: (a) Four reasons why countries engage in world trade: (i) Uneven distribution of natural resources, e.g minerals (ii) Differences in climate resulting in production of different crops in different countries (iii) The need to generate foreign exchange (iv) Differences in technical know-how and expertise for the production of mechanised goods a electronics. (b) (i) Minerals which are not found in Nigeria are imported from neighbouring countries while Nigeria exports her minerals like petroleum to others which do not have it (ii) Due to differences in climate, some crops which cannot be grown in Nigeria are imported while those that can be grown are exported. But because Nigeria a her neighbours have almost the same climate, the volume of trade tends to be reduced (iii) There is reduction of t volume of trade between Nigeria and her neighbours because they do not have the technical know-how to produce goods (iii) Foreign exchange earnings between Nigeria and her neighbours is also very low because they produce almost the same types of goods or products. (c)(i) Two sea routes through which Nigeria trades with outside wo are: (a) South Atlantic route and (b) The Cape route (c)(ii) The commodity is petroleum (or crude oil)

waec-geography-theory-0133.explanation: (b) Reasons for the shallowness of rivers and lakes of the inland drainage basin are: (i) Water from these rivers always flows into Lake Chad without flowing out (ii) Silt and other weathered rock materials continue to drop into the lakes (iii) There is the high evaporation of water in the rivers and the lakes. (c) Four benefits of the lake include: (i) For irrigation purposes (ii) For fishing (iii) For transportation of goods and people (iv) For domestic and industrial uses, e.g drinking

waec-geography-theory-0134.explanation: (a) Internal trade involves the trade in goods within country while international trade is the type of tad( done between one country and another (b) Four commodities of internal trade (i) From the north are (a) Cattle and (b) Groundnut (ii) From the south a (a) Palm oil and (b) Kola (c) Factors that promote trade between Southern and Northern Nigeria are: (i) Differences in the production of certain goods. Goods produced in the North are different from goods produce in the south, hence the need to exchange goods (ii) Efficient transportation. e.g road, railway, etc. (iii) Use of the same currency (iv) Favourable price attached to the commodities involved in internal trade (d) Limitations of internal trade: (i) Long distance between point of production and point of sales (ii) Language barrier (iii) High cost of transportation (iv) Perishability of products.

waec-geography-theory-0135.explanation: (a)(i) Mixed farming; is the type of farming in which farmers grow crops and also rear animals on the sal piece of land. Farmers grow certain crops and rear animals on the same land. (ii) Plantation agriculture; involves the cultivation of a single crop over a large area of land. Modern implements like tractor, plop harrow, planters, etc, are used in plantation agriculture In most cases, cash crops especially tree crops a grown in plantation agriculture and the produce an mainly for sale. (b) Three problems facing agriculture in Nigeria are: (i) Lack of finance or credit facilities. (ii) Inadequate land due to land tenure system (iii) Lack of storage and processing facilities. (c) The problem above can be solved as follows: (i) Government ce easily grant loans to farmers (ii) Land should be rn available to prospective farmers through the land decree of 1978 (iii) Government should provide storage and processing facilities at reduced rate.

waec-geography-theory-0136.explanation: (b) Soil characteristics that have favoured the cultivation of cocoa (Zones C): (i) The land is undulating (ii) It has well drained surface (iii) It has a deep clayey and rich-in-acid soil. Soil characteristics that favoured the cultivation of groundnut (Zone A): (i) The soil has a wide plain (ii) The top soil (A - Horizon) is humus (iii) The soil is loose and sandy. Soil characteristics that favoured the cultivation of yam (ZoneB): (i) Well drained soil (ii) Soil is sandy loam (iii) It is not acidic and it is well aerated.

waec-geography-theory-0137.explanation: Four factors that encourage concentration of industries (i) Nearness to power (ii) Availability of labour (iii) Availability of good roads (ix) Nearness to market (b) The significance of concentration of industries the inhabitants of the area are (i) It leads to the production of cheaper goods (ii) It ensures specialisation (iii) Labour is easily provided (iv) It leads to exchange of ideas

waec-geography-theory-0138.explanation: (b)(i) Historical factors: These have contributed to the variation in the population density in West Africa because ancient cities that developed like Kano, Katsina, Timbuktu are due to trans-saharan trade which took place several years ago. The population of these areas grew because of natural defence during war and being the sites of traditional empires those days (ii) Agricultural activities tend to have possible effects on population distribution e.g the eastern Nigeria, part of Ashanti developed with high population because of intensive agricultural activities due to fertility of the soil, but where the land is not fertile, people tend to abandon such areas (iii) Mining; The presence of minerals in certain areas tends to attract high population because of availability of jobs and other facilities in the areas (iv) Industrialisation. People tend to move to places where there are many industries , as these will help to provide job and improve the standard of living of the people.

waec-geography-theory-0139.explanation: (b) Three ways the highlands of Africa are important: (i) They contribute to the formation of relief rainfall (ii) Minerals are found in highlands (iii) Highlands serve as sources of rivers (c) Three importance of African rivers: (i) Generation of hydro-electricity (ii) Serve as sources of water for domestic and industrial uses (iii) Fishing is done in rivers

waec-geography-theory-0140.explanation: (b)(i) The type of vegetation found in: (1) /Area wi rainfall is throughout the year is equatorial forest (ii) The type of vegetation found in areas of summer rainfall is savanna grassland (iii) As a result of continuous rainfall, the vegetation becomes evergreen with tall trees. The trees are of different layers with canopies. But due to rainfall only in summer the trees are deciduous. i.e the trees shed the leaves during the dry season so as to conserve sufficient water. Hence most of the plants found are mainly grasses.

waec-geography-theory-0141.explanation: (a) Importance of fruit farming in the Mediterranean lands include: (i) Fruits like oranges, bananas, pineapples are consumed in many homes and are also processed into various forms of juices (ii) Most of the fruits produced are for export to European market thereby generating foreign exchange (iii) It also provides employment opportunities to people (iv) Provides raw materials for canning and processing industries (v) Wine is obtained from processing of vines which are produced in the Mediterranean lands. (b) The predominance of lumbering in Zaire basin. (i) The dense equatorial forest is a source of valuable timber (50%) of Zaire is forested) (ii) River Zaire and its numerous tributaries provide means of transporting the logs to sawmills or to ports for export (iii) There is ready market for the sawn timber both internally and externally (iv) There is high demand for timber as fuel (c) The importance of plantation agriculture in East Africa (i) Local people learn new skills in the job as machine operators, seed planters etc (ii) It provides employment opportunities to the people (iii) Plantation agriculture helps in bringing about general development in the area where it is practised

waec-geography-theory-0142.explanation: (a) Three achievements of ECOWAS since its formation (i) There is now free movement of people between the countries as travel visas for visits not lasting more than three months were abolished in 1979 (ii) Border dispute between Benin and Togo was resolved in the spirit of ECOWAS in 1975 (iii) The ECOWAS games held in Lagos in 1977 aided understanding and solidarity among the states (b) Five problems facing ECOWAS in the achievement of its objectives (i) The division of West African states along linguistic lines (English and French) discourages the coming together of the two groups. (ii) Many of the states are unable to pay their annual dues. This makes the running of the secretariat difficult. (iii) The smaller and poor countries fear that the bigger and richer ones will dominate them economically and politically (iv) Some of the richer countries are also suspicious that their resources might be tapped to enrich poorer countries (v) The countries as they become independent adopted their own different currencies. This has complicated trade

waec-geography-theory-0143.explanation: (a) Three effects of rotation of the earth include: (i) It causes day and night (ii) It causes the deflection of winds and ocean currents (iii) It causes the rising and falling of the tides. (b)(i) Reasons why all areas north of the Arctic cycle have 24 hours of daylight on June 21: (i) The sun appears to move northwards on June 21 (ii) Daylight increases as one goes towards the north pole. (iii) The sun never sets at mid-summer (nature of season) (iv) The earth is inclined to the plane of the ecliptic which causes the variation in length of daylights. (b)(ii) Reasons why areas within the tropics have more sunshine than areas outside the tropics (i) The sun is always overhead at the tropics (ii) It represents the centre of the earth (iii) It is the region which only experiences equal day and night (equinoxes) (iv) There is variation in length of day and night towards the poles.

waec-geography-theory-0144.explanation: (a)(i) River Capture: This is also called river piracy or river beheading. It results when a river through head water of erosion into a water divide cuts up the headwater of another but a weaker river. The river pirated is called misfit and the point of capture is called elbow of capture The valley below the elbow is called wind gap. (i) Waterfall: This is formed as a result of unequal resistance of hard and soft rocks transverse by a river. The out crop of a band of hard rock may cause a river to fall downstream in greater dimension from some heights called waterfall (b) One way in which river capture is useful to man is channelization of water away from settlements while waterfall is useful for the generation of hydro-electric power

waec-geography-theory-0145.explanation: Equatorial climate Tropical continental climate (a) Location 0 - 10°N and South Amazon basin (South America), Zaire, coasts of West Africa Malaysia, Indonesia, Colombia -10 - 30°N and South West Africa (North) -East Africa, Brazil, North Australia, - Orinoco basin (South America) (b) Temperature characteristics. (i) Mean annual temperature = 27°C (ii) Annual temperature range = 2°C (iii) Uniformity of temperature throughout the year - Mean annual temperature = 21°C - Annual temperature range = 9°C - Alternating hot, rainy season and cool dry season (c) Rainfall distribution (i) Rainfall is throughout the year (ii) Mean annual rainfall = 240cm (iii) It has double maxima of rainfall - Rainfall is seasonal Mean annual rainfall = 85cm - It has only single maximum of rainfall

waec-geography-theory-0146.explanation: (a) Ecosystem; is defined as the relationship between the living things and the non-living things in a community. The living things are referred to as the biotic factors while the non-living things are the abiotic factors. Examples of biotic factors are plants and animals which can be producers or consumers, while the abiotic factors include temperature, wind, rainfall, sunlight, etc. Food chain refers to the linear feeding relationships among certain species of a community. Food chain can lead to energy transfer from one organism to another. Examples of a food chain is Grass →Grasshoppers →Toads→ Hawks Grass is the producer while grasshopper, toad and hawks are consumers (b) The interdependence of the biotic and abiotic components of the environment; (i) Plants (biotic) depend on oxygen (abiotic) for respiration (ii) Plants (biotic) also depend on carbon dioxide (non biotic) for photosynthesis (iii) Plants (biotic) also depend on water (abiotic) for nutrition and other uses (iv) Plants also require sunlight for photosynthesis (v) Abiotic factors like oxygen, carbon dioxide are produced by plants and animals during photosynthesis and respiration respectively.

waec-geography-theory-0147.explanation: (a) Deforestation: This is the process of cutting down trees or forest for the purpose of farming, lumbering, mining, grazing, etc without immediate replanting of trees. Effects of deforestation include: (i) It exposes the soil to rain and wind erosion (ii) It destroys the natural forest which is rich in natural resources (iii) It could lead to flooding and desertification. Control include (i) Afforestation: which is the planting of new trees (ii)Avoiding over-grazing (iii)Avoiding indiscriminate bush burning (iv) Use of forest guards. (b) Drought: This is also called dryness. It occurs when there is-no rainfall or when it is inadequate with increase in temperature. It causes heat and dusty environment, poor yield of crops and desert encroachment. Control is by irrigation, mulching of the ground to conserve water, planting of trees, creation of shelter belts, etc

waec-geography-theory-0148.explanation: (a) Migration is the movement of people from one geographical area tc another involving permanent or temporary settlement. Three forms of migration are: (i) Rural-Urban migration (ii) Urban-Rural migration (iii) Urban-Urban migration (b) Four factors that may be responsible for migration include: (i) Physical conditions like climate, relief, etc (ii) Natural disasters like famine, floods, etc (iii) Insecurity e.g war (iv) Differences in the availability of social amenities (c) Three advantages or Rural-Urban Migration: (i) reduced population pressure on agricultural lands (ii) Supply of migrant labour (iii) Promotion of cultural integration. Three disadvantages of Rural-Urban Migration: (i) It leads to unemployment (ii) It leads to high cost of living (iii) There is pressure on social amenities.

waec-geography-theory-0149.explanation: 3. The relative contributions of roads and railways to national development in U.S.A (i) Increased agricultural,mineral and industrial production (ii) It aids the movement of people from one place to another (iii) It links areas of production with areas of consumption (iv) It leads to increased trade between towns (v) It generates revenue (vi) It leads to diffusion of ideas and innovations (vii) It promotes employment opportunities.

waec-geography-theory-0150.explanation: (a) Manufacturing industry involves the turning of raw materials into new products by mechanical or chemical processes at home or in the factory. (b) The characteristic features of manufacturing industries in tropical African countries: (i) Importation of skilled labour (ii) Imported raw materials (iii)They are labour intensive (iv) They are largely small-scaled (v) The industries are concentrated in few locations (c) Four reasons why countries embark on industrialization include: (i) To reduce over dependence on imported goods (ii) It acts as a source of revenue (iii) To generate employment (iv) To improve the standard of living.

waec-geography-theory-0151.explanation: (a) Trade between Nigeria and United Kingdom and that between Nigeria and Japan. Similarities: (i) There is importation of finished products from both countries (ii) There is export of primary products to both countries (iii) There is importation of skilled labour from both countries (iv) There is importation of technology from both countries. Differences: (i) There is older trade relationship with U.K than Japan (ii) There is greater volume of trade with the U.K (iii) Exportation of crude oil to Japan and none to U.K (iv) Importation of finished goods to Nigeria from Japan than U.K

waec-geography-theory-0152.explanation: (i) Station: A belongs to the tropical continental (or Sudan) climate while station B belongs to the sub-equatorial climate (ii) Main climatic characteristics of station A: (a)It has a high temperature throughout the year (b) The maximum temperature is 33°C while the minimum is 24°C (c) Annual temperature range is 9°C (d) Rainfall is seasonal. Main climatic characteristics of station B: (a) The temperature is high throughout the year (b) Maximum temperature is 29°C while the minimum is 23°C (c) The annual range of temperature is 6°C (d) It has a double maxima (iii) Ways in which agricultural practices in the two stations differ include (a) Rainfall is used throughout the year in station B while irrigation is used in station A (b) Cereals are mainly cultivated in station Awhile tree crops are cultivated in station B (C) Animal rearing is common in station A than in station B (d) Double cropping is done in station Awhile single cropping is done in station B

waec-geography-theory-0153.explanation: (b) Four factors that have favoured the development of internal trade include: (i) Wide demand for such goods (ii) Good transportation network (iii) Favourable climate for the cultivation of the crops (iv) Differences in products

waec-geography-theory-0154.explanation: (a) (i) Ways by which advanced technology has affected world population: (i) Provision of social amenities. (ii) Increased agricultural research. (iii) improved varieties of crops and animals. (iv) Proper waste disposal. (v) Development of chemicals to control pests (vi) Improved technology in food processing. (vii) Improved storage facilities. (viii) Development of chemicals to control diseases and improve yield. (ix) Development of fertilizers to improve fertility of soils (x) Early maturing and high yielding crops. (xi) Provision of efficient farming equipment. (xii)Establishment of Industries to provide employment opportunities. (xiii) Leads to environmental pollution (xiv) Manufacturing of weapons of destruction. (xv) Harmful effects of pesticides and insecticides on health. (xvi) Improved standard of living. (xvii) Improved irrigation and drainage facilities to support all year farming. (ii) Ways by which improved medical care has affected world population: (i) Increased population through increase in birth over deaths. (ii) increased population of causes of many diseases. (iii) Adoption of family planning techniques (iv) Extended lifespan of people. (v) Reduction in infant mortality. (vi) Improved sanitation. (vii) Availability of qualified medical personnel. (viii) Increased knowledge of prevention of diseases immunization. (ix)Availability of modern medical facilities/research. waec-geography-theory-0155.explanation: (b) Importance of crude oil to the economy of Nigeria; (i) Crude oil provides essential products like petrol and kerosine (ii) It provides employment to Nigerians (iii) It also provides raw materials for industries (iv) It provides foreign exchange for the nation (v) Provision of infrastructure like pipe borne water, good roads, electricity, etc (c) Four problems facing the mining industry in Nigeria include; (i) Environmental pollution (ii) It leads to loss of farmlands (iii) Lack of skilled labour (iv) Inadequate transport facilities

waec-geography-theory-0156.explanation: (a) Five problems of development in the Niger Delta region include: (i) Problem of soil erosion to environment (ii) Oil pollution and oil spillage are major problems (iii) High level of salt inhibits agriculture (iv) There is poor water transportation development (v) It has a very low population. (b) Solutions to the problems include: (i) Floods and erosion should be controlled (ii) Adequate care should be taken to avoid oil spillage on water (iii) The land should be reclaimed from marshy areas (iv) Flyovers should be constructed (iv) Provision of basic amenities for the people

waec-geography-theory-0157.explanation: (a) Permanent drought is the complete absence of precipitation in an area. There is virtually no water in the soil. This is common in deserts. Seasonal drought is the type in which an area only experiences drought at a particular season and plenty of rainfall or precipitation at the other season. E.g Some areas could have rainfall during the rainy season while they will experience dryness during the dry season. This situation results in seasonal drought. (b)(i) Two causes of drought are; (i) Absence of precipitation or rainfall (ii) Shifting of climatic zones which results in southwards creeping of the Sahara Desert. (ii) Two effects of drought are; (i) Drought gives rise to large scale disruption of socio-economic life due to crop failure, lack of water and livestock pasture (ii) It can lead to displacement of settlement and migration of people from drought—affected areas to other areas. (c) Two methods of minimizing the effects of drought are: (i) The application of large scale irrigation to water the area so as to stimulate the growth of vegetation (ii) Afforestation: the planting of trees minimizes the level of drought as this could even result in the formation of rain.

waec-geography-theory-0158.explanation: (a)(i) How improved medical care affected world population:- It has helped to increase population through (i) knowledge of the causes of infectious diseases and how to prevent them (ii) Provision of improved health service through availability of well-trained medical personnel (iii) Knowledge of better sanitation (iv) Reduced infant mortality rate as a result of better care. (a)(ii) How advanced technology and industry affected world population. It has led to increased population through: (i) Modernization of Agriculture, leading to plentiful and varied food supply (ii) The use of fertilizers from industries ensures the availability of food hence increase in population. (iii) Provision of storage and processing - facilities ensure the availability of food (either raw or processed form) all year round (iv) Knowledge of prevention ar control of pests and diseases which helps to increase food production (v) Provision of consumable goods from industries which ensure high standard of living. (b) Four factors which account for the high density of population in Java are: (i) Presence of rich volcanic soil (i.e tr soil is very fertile) (ii) Abundance of rainfall which ensures smooth agricultural activities (iii) Intensive agricultural activities attract people to the area (they grow 2-3 crops in a year) (iv) Favourable climate conducive for intensive farming

waec-geography-theory-0159.explanation: (a) Two types of urban settlements are: (i) Conurbation and (ii) Megalopolis (b) Characteristics of conurbation: (i) It is made up of two or more towns (ii) The towns are joined together (iii) towns still retain their identity Characteristics of megalopolis: (i) It is made up of many cities (iii) The cities a joined together (iii) It represents the largest urban settlement (c) Four problems facing urban centres are (i) Inadequate transport facilities as a result of increasing number of people trooping into urban centres (ii) Over-use and deterioration of available social amenities such as water, electrical school, etc (iii) Increase in the rate of crime as a result of lack of employment of able-bodied persons (iv) The problem of undue increase in human and vehicular traffic in urban areas.

waec-geography-theory-0160.explanation: (a) Three advantages of water transportation are: (i) Water transportation is the cheapest means of moving people and goods from one place to another: (ii) Large quantities of goods can be carried at a time over a long distance (ii) Oceans are free for use by all nations as there are no track to maintain except when approaching par Three limitations of water transportation are: (i) It is very slow (ii) Prevalence of rapids and waterfalls make inland water transportation very difficult (iii) Fluctuations in the volume of water in inland waterways makes navigation a big problem. (b) Three ways in which the limitations identified in (a) can be overcome include (i) Building of modern ships wit greater speed (ii) Efforts should be made to eliminate the cataracts and rapids along inland navigation to ensure smooth movement of ships (iii) Dredging of some important inland navigation water-ways should be done in order to ensure deep and large volume of water in these rivers.

waec-geography-theory-0161.explanation: (b)(i) YORUBA: The effects of the physical environment and type of house in Yoruba land are: (i) Yorubas are mainly involved in farming, weaving, carving, etc. - Their houses are made of mud. - Thatched houses and modern buildings are also seen in urban areas (ii) FULANI: The effects of the physical environment and type of house in Fulani are : (i) Fulanis are mainly involved in cattle rearing, farming and trading (ii) Their houses are made of mobile tents made of grass and leaves, no permanent shelter or houses

waec-geography-theory-0162.explanation: (a) Five factors responsible for the low population in some parts of WestAfrica include: (i) Historical factors like war and slavery (ii) Unfavourable climate in Northern part of West Africa (iii) Problems of pests and diseases (iv) Presence of relief, e.g eastern highlands (v) Lack of mineral resources and social amenities (b)Advantages of low population density (i) It leads to high standard of living (ii) Adequate food supply (iii) Low pressure on social amenities (iv) Low crime rate

waec-geography-theory-0163.explanation: (a) Five distinguishing features of plantation agriculture in East Africa are: (i) It involves the growing of one crop on the same piece of land (ii) A large area of land in required (iii) It requires high capital investment (iv) Cash crops are mainly involved (v)All farm operations are mechanized (b) Five factors which have favoured the practice of plantation agriculture in East Africa include: (i) Favourable climate (ii) Rich fertile soils (iii) High demands for crops (market) (iv) Availability of cheap labour (v) Good transportation system

waec-geography-theory-0164.explanation: (b) Four major problems facing landlocked countries in Africa are: (i) There is economic dependence on other countries (ii) There is loss of revenue due to smuggling (iii) There is also the problem of political insecurity (iv) There is high cost of freight rate

waec-geography-theory-0167.explanation: (a) Reasons why the production of consumer goods is common in developing countries: (i) Inadequate capital/less capital intensive (ii) Requires limited posser supply (iii) High demand for consumer goods. waec-geography-theory-0168.explanation: (a) Economic importance of oceans to man include: (i) Oceans serve as a means of transportation and communication (ii) They serve as sources of food, e.g fish, crayfish, etc. (iii) Oceans, e.g continental shelf provide minerals like petroleum and natural gas (iv) Oceans provide employment to many people e.g fishermen, sailors etc (v) Extraction of both domestic and industrial salts (b) One warm current in the North Atlantic Ocean is Floride current. Factors responsible for its movement include: (i) Planetary winds. These winds by their nature blow across oceans resulting in the movement of water (ii) The rotation of the earth (iii) Differences in temperature (iv) The shape of the land masses (v) Salinity of the water

waec-geography-theory-0170.explanation: (a)(i) The three climatic belts recognised by the Greek system of classification include: (i) Torid belt (ii) Temperate belt (iii) Frigid belt (iii) The basis of classification is temperature (b) One characteristic of each of the belts: (i) Torrid belt: It is found in the tropics with high temperatures throughout the year (ii) Temperate belt: It has a seasonal contrast in temperature (iii) The frigid belt has very low temperature throughout the year. (c) Three advantages of Koppen's classification over the Greek system include: (i)It is simple to understand (ii) It is objective (iii) It is commonly used in teaching at different levels of educational institutions.

waec-geography-theory-0171.explanation: (a) Characteristics of natural vegetation associated with the tropical continental climate: (i) The dominant vegetation cover is grass (ii) Presence of tall grasses that are fibrous when old (iii) The trees are deciduous, i.e they sheath, leaves during the dry season to reduce transpiration (iv) Presence of short scattered trees (b) Favourable factors for this type of vegetation include: (i) Low rainfall of about 600-1500cm per annum (ii) Extremes of temperature which ranges from 21-32°C (iii) It has an annual temperature range of 11°C (v) It has high monthly temperature of about 27°C (v) The vegetation has a single maximum of rainfall

waec-geography-theory-0172.explanation: (a) Five causes of flooding include: (i) Excessive rainfall (ii) Poor drainage system or lack of culverts (iii) Erection of buildings on watershed (iv) Inadequate urban planning (v) Erection of week dams and embankments (b) Four ways of controlling floods include: (i) Channelization of flood from city centres (ii) Public enlightenment on effects of flooding (ii;) Construction of wider culverts or good drainage system (iv) Installation of strong dams to act as flood reservoirs

waec-geography-theory-0173.explanation: (a) Map of Nigeria showing : (i) Major road from Lagos to Portharcourt (ii) Railway line from Lagos to Kano. (b) Contributions of transportation to the economic development of Nigeria: (i) Movement of people (ii) Movement of goods (iii) Creation of job opportunities (iv) Promote internal trade (v) Promote international trade (vi) Income to workers (vii) promotes national integration (viii) opening up new areas for development (ix) Linkages between areas of transactions (areas of production & areas of consumption) (x) Revenue generation for government (.xi) Infrastructural development (xii) Promotion of tourism (xiii) Diffusion of ideas' and innovations (xiv) Enhancement of production/GNP (xv) improvement in standard of living (xvi) Access to natural resources (xvii) Helps in the of growth of settlement (xviii) Ease of administration (xix) foreign exchange earnings (xx) Diversification of the economy. (c) Problems limiting rail transportation ill Nigeria: (i) Slow speed (ii) Narrow gauge (iii) Low patronage (iv) High cost of construction (v) Poor management (vi) Inadequate skilled technicians (vii) High cost of maintenance (viii) Competition with other means of transportation (ix) Poor maintenance (x) Old/outdated coaches (xi) Poor time schedules (xii) Difficult terrain (xiii) Derailment due to flooding (xiv) Poor communication leading to accidents (xv) Scarcity of spare parts (xvi) Railways do not have wide coverage/non-flexibility (not flexible) (xvii) Trains can only interchange at stations/single track (xviii) Low level of agricultural and other industrial productions (xix) Lack of political will/inconsistency in government policies (xx) Inadequate capital (xxi) Dwindling of mineral reserves (xxii) Low level of technology

waec-geography-theory-0174.explanation: (a) Significance of minerals as environmental resources include: (i) It provides fuel, e.g petroleum, coal and natural gas (ii) It provides foreign exchange (iii) Provision of employment, i.e mining (iv) Provision of basic amenities where mining is carried out (v) Provision of raw materials for industries, e.g limestone for cement industries (vi) Some are valuable minerals used in making necklace, wrist watches e.g gold. (b) Three major problems resulting from the exploitation of mineral resources include: (i) Environmental pollutions (ii) Depletion off natural vegetation (iii) Mining activities do lead to soil erosion

waec-geography-theory-0175.explanation: (a) Four benefits of a fall in birth rate include: (i) High per capita income (ii) High standard of living (iii) Adequacy of available social amenities and services for the people (iv) Abundant food supply for the few people (b) Four problems resulting from a fall in the birth rate of a country include: (i) Inadequate skilled and unskilled labour (ii) Low rate of exploitation of natural resources (iii) Low rate of economic development (iv) High dependency ratio, i.e. more of aged people than young ones (c) Four ways of increasing the birth rate include: (i) Encouragement of early marriages (ii) Legislation in favour of abortion (iii) Provision of benefits for single parents (iv) Government incentives such as free medical care.

waec-geography-theory-0176.explanation: (a) Five functions urban centres perform for rural areas include: (i) Processing of raw materials from rural areas (ii) Market for products from rural areas (iii) Administrative centres for rural areas (iv) Provision of employment for rural migrants (v) Provision of social services e.g higher education (b) Four problems that may limit the performance of the above functions include: (i) Inadequate communication network between urban and rural areas (ii) Inadequate jobs in the urban centres (iii) Inadequate capital for processing (iv) Political discrimination

waec-geography-theory-0177.explanation: (a) Four ways in which water transportation is important to international trade (i) It covers long distance (ii) It is very cheap (iii) It can carry bulky goods (iv) It aids transportation of passengers (b) Four limitations include: (i) Water transportation is too slow for passengers and perishable goods (ii) Presence of waterfalls and cataracts (iii) Ports may be silted up or frozen (iv) Problems of sea weeds or water hyacinth (c) The above limitations can be overcome by (i) Continuos dredging (ii) Improved technology (iii) Continuous clearing of sea weeds (iv) Construction of canals to bypass falls

waec-geography-theory-0178.explanation: (a) Five factors for the location of cement factory include: (i) Presence of raw materials e.g limestone (ii) Presence of large market (iii) Source of power e.g H.E.P (iv) Availability of capital (v) Adequate transportation networks (b) Three problems facing cement factories are: (i) Inadequate capital to procure machinery (ii) Inadequate spare parts to service machines (iii) Inadequate transportation network.

waec-geography-theory-0179.explanation: (a) Inter-dependence in trade between Nigeria and Britain include: (i) Differences in physical setting, e.g climate (ii) Differences in products - agricultural and manufactured goods (iii) The need to earn foreign exchange (iv) Colonial linkage (b) Four factors limiting the trade include: (i) Inadequate production of goods (ii) Low demand for products (iii) Political instability (iv) High tariffs on goods (c) Three ways of improving the trade include: (i) Increased production by both countries (ii) Membership of the same international economic organisation (iii) Increased international co-operation between both countries

waec-geography-theory-0180.explanation: (b) Four physical factors limiting the use of rivers for transportation include: (i) Presence of waterfall and rapids (ii) Problems of water weed (iii) Fluctuating volume of water due to seasons (iv) Short length of rivers (c) The above problems can be overcome by (i) Construction of dams (ii) Continuos clearing of water weeds (iii) Dredging of rivers (iv) Construction of canal

waec-geography-theory-0181.explanation: A Geographical account of the Cross River Plains under the following headings: (a) Climate: (i) Sub-equatorial (ii) Rainfall all throughout the year (iii) Rainfall is heavy (iv) Rainfall is over 3000 mm per annum has double maxima rainfall (v) Mean annual temperature is between 21°C—30°C (vi) Daily temperatures ranges between 2°C -- 3°C (viii) Prevailing winds are south west trade winds (ix) Cloudy skies (x) High relative humidity of over 80% (xi) Rainfall is convectional accompanied with thunder and lightening. (b)Economic activities: (i) Fishing (ii) Farming (iii) Tourism (iv) Industrial activities (v)Communication (vi) centre (vii) for education research (viii) Government job (ix) Hospitality industry (x) Commerce/trading (xii) Mining (xiii) Lumbering (xiv) Transport operations. (xi) Local craft (c) Problems of development: (i)environmental degradation (ii) loss of grazing lands (iii) loss of drinking water (iv) resettlement problems (v) occupational dislocation (vi) conflicts over sharing of resettlement allowances (vii) health problems/diseases (viii) pollution (ix) poor transport network (x) inadequate landmass for development (xi) youth restiveness (xii) mismanagement (xiii) pests (xiv) soil erosion/leaching (xv) occasional flooding/poor drainage (xvi) sparse population/dispersed settlement (xvii) inadequate infrastructure

waec-geography-theory-0182.explanation: (b) Characteristics of Guinea Savanna; (i) Presence of tall trees (ii) Presence of tall grasses (iii) Trees shed their leaves during the dry season (iv) Trees found include locust beans, shea-butter (c) Relationship between the rainfall and vegetation in the Savanna include: (i) Rainfall decreases from the Guine2 Savanna towards the Northern limit (ii) Rainfall duration is longer in the Guinea Savanna than the Sahel Savanna (iii) Little rainfall of between 20cm - 7cm in the Sahel leads to stunted growth of trees (iv) Arrival of rainfall marks the beginning of the grasses in the savanna.

waec-geography-theory-0183.explanation: (a) Reasons for market gardening in urban areas include: (i) Produce are in high demand - such as vegetable, fruits, etc. (ii) The need to be close to a large market (iii) It does not need a large expanse of land (iv) Presence of good network of routes (b) Lumbering in the high forest belts: (i) Presence of suitable climatic conditions-high rainfall throughout the year (ii) Presence of forest trees (iii) Presence of varieties of species (iv) Presence of hardwood for construction purposes (c) Rice in middle belt; (i) Presence of large expanse of land due to low population (ii) Presence of adequate climatic conditions, e.g rainfall of over 125cm (iii) Abundance of swampy areas along river valley (iv) Absence of export crops.

waec-geography-theory-0184.explanation: (b) Four economic importance of North-Central Highlands include (i) Presence of mineral deposits e.g tin and columbite (ii) Rearing of cattle (iii) Source of many rivers (iv) Provision of hard rocks for construction (c) Four problems limiting the economic development of the region include: (i) Presence of rugged terrain (ii) Inadequate rainfall (iii) Soil erosion problem (iv) Scattered settlements

waec-geography-theory-0185.explanation: (b)(i) Population and settlement of Eastern Highlands -The area is sparsely populated -Population density is between 20 - 100 persons/ km2 -It has dispersed settlements (ii) Natural Resources (a) Presence of minerals (b) Presence of waterfalls (c) Presence of highlands (iii) Economic Activities (a) Crop farming (b) Animal rearing (c) Mining activities

waec-geography-theory-0186.explanation: (b) Three objectives of the ECOWAS include: (i) Increased trade between member countries (ii) Free movement of goods, services, and people (iii) Promote cooperation and development in economic activities (c) Three factors limiting the attainment of the objectives include: (i) Language barrier (ii) Strong colonial ties (iii) Similarity of economic activities.

waec-geography-theory-0187.explanation: (b) Three importance of river basins include: (i) It provides good sites for settlement (ii) It is suitable for agricultural purposes (iii) Presence of rivers serves as communication routes (c) Three characteristics of the Coastline of Africa include (i) They have few indentation (ii) It has some estuaries e.g Togo (iii) It may have delta coast, e.g Nile, Niger

waec-geography-theory-0188.explanation: (a) Effects of latitude on climate of Africa (i) Insolation if more direct at the equator and included at the tropics (ii) Rainfall amount is higher at the low latitudes than at the high latitude (iii) There is rainfall all the year round at the low latitudes and seasonal in high latitudes (b) Effects of ocean currents (i) It determines the amount of rainfall (ii) It affects rain formation (iii) It leads to coastal fogs (iv) It modifies temperature (c) Distance from the sea (i) Extremes of temperature in the interior (ii) It is higher in the interior (iii) Higher humidity along the coast (iv) It also leads to thicker cloud cover along the coast

waec-geography-theory-0189.explanation: (b) Four problems facing mining in Africa; (i) Inadequate capital (ii) High cost c production (iii) Inadequate skilled labour (iv) Fluctuation of prices of minerals

waec-geography-theory-0190.explanation: (a) Four favourable factors include; (i) Presence of fertile soils (ii) Availability of cheap labour (iii) Favourable climate (iv) Large market for produce (b) Four importance of plantation agriculture include; (i) Provision of employment (ii) It supplies cash crops (iii) It provide: raw materials for industries (iv) It provides foreign exchange (c) Four problems of plantation agriculture include: (i) Foreign ownership of farms (ii) Infestation of pests and diseases (iii) Fluctuation in prices of produce (iv) Poor transportation network

waec-geography-theory-0191.explanation: (a) Similarities of Latitude and Longitudes (i) Both are imaginary lines (ii) Both are drawn on the globe or map (iii) Both are measured in degrees (iv) Both are used for location of places or positions on the globe. (v) Both are circular in shape (b) Differences between Latitudes and Longitudes; (i) Latitudes are drawn from West to East, while longitudes a drawn from North to South (ii) Latitudes are called parallels while longitudes are called meridians (iii) Longitudes are used to calculate time, while latitudes are not (iv) Only the equator is a Great Circle among the latitudes while all lines of longitudes form Great Circles with their opposite members (v) Latitudes are parallel and never meet while longitudes converge and meet at the poles.

waec-geography-theory-0192.explanation: (a) ROCK PEDESTALS: Characteristics: It has soft and hard rock layers, mushroom with irregular shape formed in desert e.g Sahara desert The soft rock layers is eroded more rapidly resulting in the formation of irregular edge of alternate bands of hard and soft rock. Further erosion at the base produces a mushroom-shaped feature . (ii) YANDANG: This is an erosional feature formed by wind abrasion in desert e.g Atacama desert. It has vertical bands or hard and soft rocks of height between 5-15cm. Characteristics: Yandang is found in the desert. Vertical bands of hard and soft rocks standing in the direction of prevailing wind is eroded such that Rock the softer rock is eroded faster than the hard rock resulting in the formation of Yandang.

waec-geography-theory-0193.explanation: (a)(i) Explanatory Notes on Population Density: (i) Population density refers to the ratio of people per unit area. It can be expressed as Total population Total land area Population can be expressed as persons per km'. Population density could be high or low depending on the factors of increase or decrease. (ii) Explanatory Notes on Birth Rate: Birth rate refers to the number of live births per thousand persons in a population. The birth rate is presented on a yearly or annual basis. Birth rate could be high or low depending on the factors of increase or decrease. It is used to estimate the annual growth rate of a population. (iii) Explanatory notes on Optimum Population: Optimum population is the relationship between population and available resources. It is a situation where the number of people in a given area equals the resources within the area. Optimum population is a difficult situation to attain in real life. It is a situation of equilibrium. Any additional number of people leads to over population and any reduction in number of people leads to under population. This situation often involves size of population and technical competence. (b) Ways by which the Problems of Under Population can be Solved: (i) Improved welfare packages. (ii) Discouraging all forms of birth control. (iii) Public enlightenment. (iv) Discouragement of monogamy. (v) Economic support for single parents. (vi) Encouragement of early marriage. (vii) Child welfare benefits, such as monthly upkeep allowances. (viii) Encouragement of polygamy. (ix) Legislation against abortion. (x) Encouragement of immigrants. (xi) Acquisition of skills. (xii) Increase in food supply. (xiii) Government incentives, such as free medical care, education, etc. (xiv) Gainful employment.

waec-geography-theory-0194.explanation: (a)(i) Mean annual temperature = Total temperature (Jan-Dec) 12 = -19 + -17 +........ +-5+-13 12 = 1.5°C (ii) Annual range of temperature = temp of hottest month - temp of coldest month 18- (-19) = 18 + 19 = 37°C (iii) Total annual precipitation = Add total precipitation (Jan - Dec) = 27 + 17 +....... + 27 + 22 = 503mm (b) The station has single peak (June and July) and lowest precipitation is in February Total annual precipitation is 503mm. Rainfall from April to October and precipitation is throughout the year (c) The type of natural vegetation is the cost temperate grassland (or steppe) Reasons: (i) Plant growth restricted to about 5 months when temperatures are above the minimum required for grass growth (ii) It has 5 months with temperature above 6°C

waec-geography-theory-0195.explanation: (a) Location: Tropical grasslands are located in the tropics while temperate grasslands are located in temperate latitude. Again tropical grasslands are found between 10° and 30° North and South while temperate grassland are found between 30° and 40° North and South of the Equator (b) Climate: Tropical grassland has moderate rainfall (25-150cm) while temperate grassland has lower rainfall (40-50cm) Tropical grassland is not all the year round but temperate grassland has cold winter and warm summers. In tropical grassland, summer temperature is 32°C and 21°C while temperate grassland has 18°C in summer and —19°C in winter. (c) Characteristics: Tropical grassland contains scattered trees while temperate grassland is almost treeless. Trees in the tropical grassland are bigger than those of temperate-grassland.jropical grasses are tough while temperate grasses are succulent. Example of tropical grass is elephant grass while temperate grass is willow.

waec-geography-theory-0196.explanation: (a) The natural environment is the habitat where plants and animals dwell in undisturbed form or state (b) Four advantages of man's intervention with natural environment include: (i)Agricultural products for domestic and industrial uses (ii) Mineral products for industrial uses (iii) Land for settlement (iv) Water for domestic and industrial uses. Four disadvantages for man's interventions with natural environment include: (i) Depletion of mineral resources (ii) Depletion of vegetation resources (iii) Pollution of water, land and air (iv) Drought and desertification

waec-geography-theory-0197.explanation: (a)(i) Over-population is a situation where a country has more people than its physical and human resources can support with adequate living standard (ii) Migration is the movement of people on a seasonal, or permanent basis from their original location to another. (b)(i) Three factors responsible for over-population include: (a) Low level of education (b) The culture of the people/large family size) (c) High birth rate (ii) Three factors responsible for migration include; (a) Environmental hazards e.g earthquake, floods, drought (b) Low standard of living -search for greener pastures (c) Fear of insecurity e.g War, Political instability etc.

waec-geography-theory-0198.explanation: (a) Three classes of settlements based on their functions include: (i) Commercial e.g London, New York, Lagos, Accra (ii) Industrial e.g Lagos, Accra (iii) Administrative e.g Washington DC, Abuja, London (b)(i) Characteristics - Commercial settlement/town - It is a centre of exchange for goods - It is usually very accessible - it has high population concentration majority of whom are traders (ii) Administrative settlement/ town - it is centre of administration - It has high population whose population are mainly civil servants - Presence of social amenities.

waec-geography-theory-0199.explanation: (a) Modes of Transportation: (i) Road (ii) Water (iii) Air (iv) Pipeline (v) Railway (vi) Cable or rope way. (b) Constraints to Inland Water Navigation: Short courses of rivers. (ii) Low patronage. (iii) Poor management. (iv) Slow speed. (v) Fluctuations in the volume of rivers. (vi) Shallow nature of most river valleys. (vii) (viii) Adverse weather conditions. (ix) Poor maintenance culture. (x) Poor navigational aids. (xi) Limited capital. (xii) Presence of water weeds, such as water hyacinth. (xiii) Hazards of tree stumps. (xiv) Freezing of rivers and lakes. (xv) Competition with other modes of transportation. (xvi) Presence of rapids, cataracts, waterfall or dams. (xvii) Silting of river mouths. (xviii) Problem of piracy. (xix) Narrow gorges. (xx) Presence of dangerous aquatic animals. (c) Ways in which the Constraints can be Solved: (i) Provision of adequate capital. (ii) Construction canals. (iii) Removal of water machines/herbicides. (iv) Dredging of more canals for accessibility (v) Channelization to avoid rapids and waterfalls. (vi) Policing water ways. (iii) Dredging to increase depths of rivers. (viii) Improved management. (ix) Removal of tree stumps. (x) Development of the hinterland (xi) Enlightenment on the use of inland water (xii) Improving the technology Of speed boat engines to increase speed. (xiii) Introduction of comfortable boats. (xiv) Cultivation of good maintenance culture. (xv) Provision of modern navigational aids. (xvi) Traffic control on rivers to check piracy (xvii) Use of dams and reservoirs to control water levels. (xviii) Use of ice breakers. (xix) Involvement of conservation to control dangerous animals.

waec-geography-theory-0200.explanation: (a) Three reasons for preferring air transportation includes: (i) It is the fastest means of transportation (ii) It can move mails, passengers and high value cargo (iii) It can cover long distances (b) Three disadvantages of air transportation includes (i) High cost of transportation fares (ii) Air crashes are usually disastrous as chances of survival are highly limited (iii) There is problem of air terrorism (c) Solutions to the problems; (i) Government subsidy of airfares (ii) Training of flight and technical crew (iii) Security to be more enforced.

waec-geography-theory-0201.explanation: (a)(i) An example of light industry is any of the following. Matches, Paper mills, Furniture, Printing,etc. (ii) An example of heavy industry include: Iron and Steel, Ship building, Petro-Chemical (b) Four Characteristics of Light Industry: (i) It can be located anywhere (ii) It is labour intensive (iii) It produces light products (iv) It employs mostly female labour force (ii) Heavy industry: (a) Usually located near raw material or market (b) It requires heavy machines (c) It requires skilled labour (d) It also requires large capital outlay. (c) Three factors which aided the location of one of the industries include: (i) Raw materials (ii) Market (iii) Transportation; others include labour supply, power supply, availability of capital etc.

waec-geography-theory-0202.explanation: (a) Four advantages of international trade: (i) Provision of foreign exchange earning to government (ii) Generation of employment (iii) Healthy diplomatic or bilateral relations (iv) Mutual exchange of technical and other services (b) Four factors which influence the trade between Nigeria and Canada: (i) Differences in natural resources (ii) Tariffs and import duties chargeable (iii) Degree of industrial development or level of technology (iv) Differences in taste

waec-geography-theory-0203.explanation: (a)(i) Map of Nigeria showing three climatic belts (ii) The dominant air mass (a) Tropical Maritime air mass and (b) Tropical continental air mass Three adaptation of Sudan savanna to climate of Nigeria (i) Trees have long tap roots which reach ground water during dry season. (ii) Shedding of leaves in the dry season (iii) Thorny leaves to control rate of evapo-transpiration (c) Four economic importance of vegetation to man include: (i) Provision of food e.g fruits, seeds etc for man (ii) Provision of food for animals (iii) Provision of raw materials for industrial purposes e.g twines, ropes (iv) Provision of employment and fuel.

waec-geography-theory-0204.explanation: (a) Four problems facing Agriculture in Nigeria include: (i) Inadequate labour - rural depopulation - drift to the towns/ mines etc leaving old people on the farm (ii) Land tenure system giving rise to fragmentation of farm holding (iii) Inadequate capital (iv) Use of crude implements e.g hoe, cutlass etc. (b) Three effects of the above problems on the economic development of Nigeria are: (i) High prices of agricultural products (ii) Shortage of foods (ii) Reduction of income to farmers/government (c) Solutions to the above problems in (a); (i) Improvement of rural areas by government (ii) Introduction of land reforms (iii) Granting !cans to farmers (iv) Provision of tractors, plough harrow at reduced price

waec-geography-theory-0205.explanation: (b) Four contributions of railway to the economic development of Nigeria include: (i) Transportation of manufactured goods (ii) Evacuation of agricultural goods (iii) Generation of income to government (iv) Provision of employment to people. (c) Three problems of rail transportation in Nigeria include: (i) Slow speed of rail (ii) Inadequate capital (iii) Poor management of rail transport

waec-geography-theory-0206.explanation: (a) Relief and drainage (i) The Chad basin is a low-lying area of an average elevation of 45-60m above the sea-level. It is poorly drained and rivers flow into the Lake Chad e.g Hadeija, Gana and Yobe rivers (b) Agriculture: Farming types include fishing, cattle rearing, irrigation, arable farming, mixed farming etc. Products of agriculture include food crops like groundnut, vegetables, beans, rice, millet, etc while animal products include beef, milk, hides and skin, fish etc (c) problems of development include: Drought, desert encroachment, inadequate natural resources, soil erosion, inadequate capital and low level of technology.

waec-geography-theory-0207.explanation: Eastern scarpland Western Highlands (a) Relief (i) Scarplands with average elevation of about 300m above the sea level (ii) Alternating Plateau and Cuestas separated by wide Manu-Oji river valley (iii) Made up of sandstones eg. Udi hills - Curved ridges higher than Eastern Scarpland average elevation between 300-600m above the sea level. - It is heavily dissected by rivers - Made up of granites eg Idanre hills (b) People and population: (i) Tribes are Igbo, Igala (ii) Population density of over 200 persons/sq km (iii) Simple dressing Largely Yoruba Over 200 persons per sq km Voluminous way of dressing (c) Settlement patterns; (i) Mainly rural (ii) Nucleated (iii) Few linear settlement Highly urbanised Nucleated More linear settlement (d) Agriculture; (i) Food crops include yam, coco-yarn, cassava maize, rice (ii) Cash crops, e.g Oil-palms, citrus, cashew nuts (iii) Livestock farming -goatS, sheep, Ndama cattle Casava, rice, yam, maize, plantain Cocoa, rubber, citrus, coffee, oil palm, kola nuts Coat, chicken, sheep, Muturu cattle

waec-geography-theory-0208.explanation: (a) (i) Characteristic Features of Conurbation: (1) It is an urban settlement. (2) Two or more large cities/ towns merge to form Conurbation. (3) The big cities are merged together by rapid population (4) The big cities are linked by efficient and physical expansion but with different identities. transportation system/network. (5) The big cities form one large market for industries. trade and transport. (6) It is a continuous built-up area. (7) Has a high population density. (8) Its population is much greater than that of the nearby towns. (9) It has various industries operating in it (10) It relies on the reserves of labour, excellent transport, Medicare, etc. (11) Conurbation as a shopping centre due to the cheap and excellent transport facilities. (12) It has a unique financial strength. (13) Examples: Lagos, Accra, Ruhr Valley,Tokyo. Monrovia, Serreaunda. (ii) Characteristic Features of Megapolis: (1) It is also called megalopolis/mega city/super city. (2) The highest category of settlement. (3) Has large territories consisting of great conurbations. (4) It is highly urbanized region. (5)A very large city with population of more than 10 million inhabitants. (6) An urban complex. (7) Continuous built-up area. (8) Linked with communication(transport networks. (9) Examples: North East USA, Lagos (Nigeria), Cairo (Egypt). New Delhi (India). (b) Functions of Settlements: (1) It has commercial functions, e.g. Onitsha (Nigeria).Kano (Nigeria). New York (U.S.A.), Kumasi (Ghana), etc. (2) Administrative function. e.g. Abuja (Nigeria). Addis Ababa (Ethiopia). etc. (3) Religious function, e.g. Mecca. Rome. Lhasa. Banares (India). (4) Mining function. e.g. Jos. Enugu. (5) Educational function. e.g. Ibadan. Ilorin. Benin City, Accra. Kumasi, Oxford. Obuasi. Johannesburg. (6) Military functions, e.g. Jaji, Kaduna, Portmouth. Wilberforce, etc. (7) Industrial function. e.g. Port Harcourt. Takoradi, Tema, Lagos, Freetown, Birmingham. (8) Port function. e.g. Lome, Lagos, Tenia. Banjul. Freetown. (9) Royal function, e.g. Ile-lfe. Benin City (Nigeria). London (U.K.). Sokoto (Nigeria). (10) Resort function, e.g. Miami (Florida). Obudu, Yankari, Matnbila (Nigeria). (11) Residential!satellite function. e.g. Amuwo (Lagos), Nyanya (Abuja), Harlow (U.K.)

waec-geography-theory-0209.explanation: (a) Reasons for high volume of trade between Nigeria and Japan include (i) Goods produced by both countries ar different hence the increase in the volume of trade (ii) Differences in climatic conditions create the conditions necessary for the production of different agricultural goods (iii) Differences in the level of technology (iv) Increase foreign exchange earnings (v) Increase in the prices of goods offered for sale.

waec-geography-theory-0210.explanation: (a) Three broad classes of manufacturing industries are (i) Cottage or craft industries e.g West Africa (ii) Light industries e.g India (iii) Heavy industries e.g USA. (b)(i) Three main characteristics of cottage or craft industry (i) It involves very few people working at home (ii) It not require power-driven machines (iii) Special skills are required. (bii) Three characteristics of light industries (i) They produce relatively small light weigh goods (ii) Products are mainly final or consumer goods (iii) They usually employ a lot of female workers (biii) Three characteristics of heavy industries (i) They produce heavy and bulky goods (ii) Products are neither final nor consumer goods but are used in construction or manufacturing industries (iii) they usually employ male workers due to the nature of work involved.

waec-geography-theory-0211.explanation: (b) Seasonal pattern of rainfall in Southern Nigeria; (i) The long wet season - Rainfall starts in March till July when plants look green due to heavy rains and high humidity (ii) The short dry season - Called the August break where there is little or no rainfall in the month of August (iii) The short wet season- Starts from August ending October. The rainfall is not heavy as the first season (iv) The long dry, or harmattan season -Starts around November till mid-March with cool and misty morning, hazy afternoon and a cold and dry evening. There is virtually no rainfall during this time. (c) The effects of seasonal pattern of rainfall on farming activities include (i) it enables farmers to grow crops in a year (ii) it enables farmers to grow tree crops because of heavy rainfall (iii) Harvesting of crops is usually done especially during the dry season (iv) Heavy rainfall however, discourages livestock farming because it does not favour grass growth.

waec-geography-theory-0212.explanation: (a) Areas of fishing in Nigeria include the following: (i) Inland fishing areas like rivers, Lake Chad and streams (ii) Fishing in creeks and lagoons (iii) Ocean or off-shore fishing (b) Methods of fishing include: (i) The use of traps (ii) The use of hooks and lines (ii) The use of nets (iv) The use of trawlers in ocean fishing (c) Types of fish include: Tilapia, Catfish, Claris, Shark, Mackerel, etc. (d) Importance of fishing in Nigeria: (i) Provision of food, it is a source of protein (ii) It provides employment to many people (iii) Fish exported can provide foreign exchange (iv) Fish by-products are used as fish meal in livestock farming (v) Establishment of fish processing industries.

waec-geography-theory-0213.explanation: (b) Major causes of desertification include: (i) Shifting of climatic zones e.g natural shifting or encroachment of the Sahara Desert towards the North estimated to be 50km per year (ii) Climatic variations - very low rainfall (iii) Human activities such as deforestation and overgrazing (c) Two possible ways of combating desert encroachment include: (i) Large scale irrigation system - This will enable water to be available in the soil and consequently promote the growth of vegetation in the area. (ii) Afforestation - This involves the planting of trees which act as barriers to the speed of winds carrying sand from the desert

waec-geography-theory-0228.explanation: (a) Four factors that determine population distribution are; (i) Climate: temperature extremes, i.e too high and too low temperature lead to sparse population while moderate temperature leads to dense population (ii) Relief; Low relief leads to dense population while rugged relief leads to sparse population (iii) Minerals: Presence of minerals leads to high population while absence of minerals leads to low population (iv) Soil: Fertile soil attracts dense population while poor soils attract low population (b) Two types of population movement are: (i) Rural-Urban Movement (ii) Urban-Rural Movement (c) Four problems of Rural-Urban migration (i) Population pressure on land (ii) Congestion (traffic, housing) (iii) Increase in crime wave (iv) Unemployment

waec-geography-theory-0238.explanation: (a) Five features of rotational bush fallowing are; (i) Farmlands are left to fallow after one or two years of cultivation (ii) Farmers return to the farmland after fallow period of 2-5 years (ii) It uses simple farm tools It uses family labour (v) Mixed cropping is usually practised (b) Four advantages of the system include: (i) Soil fertility is regained naturally (ii) It is easy to practice as low technology is required (iii) Fallow area provides good grazing grounds (iv) It is cheap as little is spent on labour and other inputs (c) Four advantages of the system include (i) It wastes land due to large area required (ii) It leads to land fragmentation (iii) It leads to soil erosion when soil is exhausted (iv) It does not give room for mechanization

Formation: Band of hard and soft rocks which lie parallel to the prevailing winds in the desert are turned into another type of ridge and furrow landscape by wind and abrasion (b) Block Mountains Characteristics: (i) Found in areas of ancient fold mountains (ii) Associated with rift valleys (iii) Uplifted area in the block mountain or horst (iv) Steepsided (v) Generally flat topped (vi) Examples are Ruwenzori in East Africa, Vosges Black Forest in France. Formation: When parallel vertical faults develop in the crust, they divide the land into blocks. When tensional force sets on the blocks and presses the outside block down while the middle block stands, a block mountain is formed

waec-geography-theory-0246.explanation: (a) Food plains: It is found at the lower course of a river and generally low lying. During floods, large quantities of materials are transported the upper course of the river and these materials are spread over low lying adjacent areas. 4. layer of sediments gradually builds up the flood plain usually very fertile. It is dangerous for human habitation. Examples are Ganges Plain, Mississippi, Hwang-Ho etc (b) Hydrological Cycle: This is the movement of water through a series of processes - evaporation, transportation and precipitation. When it rains, some water immediately evaporate back to the atmosphere, while some are absorbed by plants and gradually return to the atmosphere by way of transpiration. Some water run off the slopes and rivers and flow back to seas and oceans while some evaporate directly from the ground to the atmosphere. Clouds are also formed, then rains are formed in the atmosphere and water sent back to the ground and some water percolate in the ground to form ground water.

waec-geography-theory-0247.explanation: (a) Processes of Soil Formation: Soil formation takes place over a long period of time and it involves the mixture of inorganic mineral water, organic water, liquid substances, gaseous substances, and living organisms. It begins with the production of inorganic mineral matter from parent materials and also involves accumulation or organic substances. Other processes include movement of weathered products in the form of clay particles, colloids or solutions and plant nutrients through soil profile as well as action of living organisms (b) Importance of Soil; (i) Food for micro-organisms (ii) Medium for plant growth (iii) Source of materials (iv) Support for plants (v) Habitat for macro and micro organisms
